2 
 
 
 
Recommendation (Para No.2.8) 
1.5. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
 “The Committee note that the delay in adoption of procedural changes 
introduced by  the Ministry of Finance such as SNA system, PFMS by the 
State/UT Governments  resulted in under-utilisation of Budgetary/ Revised 
Estimates in 2023-24 and 2024-25.  The Committee firmly believe that 
with these procedural changes the financial  resources of the Government 
of India will not get stuck up in the State treasury and  can be fruitfully 
utilised by the Ministry of Minority Affairs on other welfare measures. 
 Since the State/UT Governments have streamlined the system by adopting the 
procedural changes, the Committee expect that the Ministry of Minority Affairs 
would be able to spend their budgetary allocation for 2024-25 on the various 
schemes for the welfare of minority communities. The Committee are, however, 
apprehensive as they feel that the actual expenditure in 2024-25 may again be 
less than the Budgetary Estimates as the approval of several Schemes of 
Ministry of Minority Affairs is at various stages. The Committee, therefore desire 
that the approval of the Schemes of the Ministry of Minority Affairs should be 
expedited so that Schemes such as Scholarship Schemes and PM-VIKAS are 
implemented without any delay, thus avoiding under-utilisation of Budgetary 
Estimates. In view of the above, the Committee, recommend that the necessary 
mechanism may be evolved so that the Schemes requiring approval is timely 
obtained so that the benefit of the Schemes reaches the deprived sections of 
the Minority Communities.” 
1.6. The Ministry of Minority Affairs, in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as 
under:- 
 “The Observations of Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance.  
PMJVK: 
The Ministry has taken pro-active steps to utilise BE allocations in respect of 
PMJVK Scheme. The expenditure till 31.01.2025 under the scheme is ₹641.41 
crore against the RE of ₹908.90 crore. Furthermore, additional amount of ₹100 
crore have been requested for in the 2nd batch of supplementary for F.Y. 2024-
25 and it is assured that the fund will be utilised fully. 
Scholarship: 
Ministry implements three scholarship schemes viz. Pre-Matric, Post Matric and 
Meritc-cum-Means for the educational empowerment of 6 centrally notified 
minority communities. Under these schemes, the scholarship amount is 
disbursed to the beneficiaries through Direct Benefits Transfer Mode under 

3 
 
Aadhar Mode Biometric System while the administrative expenses release to 
States/UTs on reimbursement basis. Hence the SNA system is not applicable in 
case of 3 scholarship schemes for minorities.  
As these schemes are yet to be approved for implementation beyond 2021-22 
neither any target fixed nor scheme could be implemented from 2022-23 
onwards. This Ministry endeavours to get these schemes approved for 
implementation beyond 2021-22 after harmonization with similar schemes of 
other Central Ministries, with approval of the Competent Authority in the 
Government at the earliest. 
PM VIKAS: 
Ministry has expedited the roll out of PM VIKAS scheme. Approval of the 
competent authority has already been obtained on the scheme of the guidelines 
of the PM VIKAS Scheme. The Ministry has started the receiving proposals from 
the eligible organisation under the scheme. Meeting of Screening Committee 
was held on 12th February,2025 to examine and discuss the proposals. The 
meeting of the Empowered Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary 
MoMA was held on 10th March,2025. On ground project implementation is 
expected to start in April,2025.” 
  
1.7. The Committee in their original Report had noted the under-
utilization of Budgetary allocation of the Ministry of Minority Affairs in 
2023-24 and 2024-25 due to  various reasons such as delay in adoption of 
procedural changes introduced by the Ministry of Finance for 
implementation of various schemes and pending approvals for continuation 
of three Scholarship Schemes namely Pre-Matric, Post-Matric and Merit-
cum-Means beyond 2021-22 because of the ongoing process of 
harmonization of these schemes with similar schemes of other 
Ministries/Departments.  The Committee had accordingly inter-alia desired 
that the approval of these schemes should be expedited without any delay 
to avoid under-utilization of Budgetary allocation. On scrutiny of the Action 
Taken Replies of the Ministry of Minority Affairs, the Committee find that 
the process of harmonization of scholarship schemes with similar schemes 
of other Central Ministries is still not complete. As these Schemes are in 
abeyance since 2022-23, the Committee strongly believe that the education 
of the students must have suffered due to non-availability of financial 
assistance to them from these Schemes. It is the strong desire of the 

4 
 
Committee that the students should not be made to suffer for no fault and 
necessary efforts should be made by the Ministry of Minority Affairs.  Since 
these scholarship schemes are crucial for educational upliftment of 
economically weaker sections of Minority communities, the Committee 
recommend that concrete steps need to be taken to complete the process 
of the harmonization in a time bound manner so that the students can avail 
the benefits of the schemes as being availed by the students of the similar 
Schemes of other Central Ministries.   
 
Recommendation (Para No.3.16) 
1.8. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee find that the Ministry of Minority Affairs implements Pre-Matric 
Scholarship Scheme, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme, Merit cum means based 
scholarship, Maulana Azad National Fellowship and Padho Pradesh Scheme for 
the educational empowerment of minority communities. The Committee, 
however, find that the Maulana Azad National Fellowship and Padho Pardesh 
Scheme have been discontinued with effect from 2022-23 and the remaining 
educational empowerment Schemes viz. Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme, Post-
Matric Scholarship Scheme are pending for approval since 2021-22. The 
Committee are of the view that education of the students belonging to minority 
communities should not be made to suffer for the administrative delays and 
necessary measures should be taken to ensure that there is no interruption in 
implementation of the Schemes. Since, the process of harmonisation of 
Scholarship Schemes of all the Ministries/ Departments is in progress, the 
Committee desire this exercise should be expedited. The Committee are aware 
that several other educational empowerment Schemes such as National 
Fellowship, National Overseas Scholarship, Free Coaching, Residential 
education, etc. are being implemented for the educational empowerment of 
various marginalised sections of the society by various Ministries/Departments. 
The Committee would, therefore, like the Ministry of Minority Affairs to examine 
the need of implementing other educational empowering schemes for the poor 
students of minority communities so that they may also avail the best of 
education and contribute in the growth of the nation. The Committee would 
also like to recommend that the Scholarship Schemes pending for approval 
should be approved without further delay.” 
 
 
 

5 
 
 
1.9. The Ministry of Minority Affairs, in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as 
under:- 
“Ministry implements three scholarship schemes viz. Pre-Matric, Post Matric and 
Meritc-m-Means for the educational empowerment of 6 centrally notified 
minority communities. As these schemes are yet to be approved for 
implementation beyond 2021-22 neither any target fixed nor scheme could be 
implemented from 2022-23 onwards. This Ministry endeavours to get these 
schemes approved for implementation beyond 2021-22 after harmonization 
with similar schemes of other Central Ministries, with approval of the Competent 
Authority in the Government at the earliest.” 
 
1.10. The Committee in their Original Report found that several schemes 
such as National Fellowship, National Overseas Scholarship, Free Coaching, 
Residential Education, etc. are being implemented without any interruption 
in other Central Ministries/Departments such as Department of Social 
Justice and Empowerment, Department of Empowerment of Persons with 
Disabilities and Ministry of Tribal Affairs.  However, these schemes have 
been discontinued by Minority Affairs.  In the absence of these schemes, 
the Ministry of Minority Affairs is depriving needy and deserving students 
of Minority communities from pursuing higher education.  The Committee 
had accordingly recommended to reconsider the decision to discontinue the 
above-mentioned educational schemes for minority communities.  The 
Committee, however, find from the Action Taken Replies of the Ministry of 
Minority Affairs that no action has been taken by the Ministry in this regard.  
The Committee firmly believe that deprived sections of the society from 
across the communities deserve to pursue higher education, hence, 
members of the Minority Community should avail same benefits as being 
provided to other marginalised sections of the society by the other Central 
Ministry/Departments. The Committee reiterate their earlier 
recommendation and desire that the Ministry of Minority Affairs should take 
affirmative action in this regard. 
 
 
 

6 
 
 
Recommendation (Para No.5.9) 
1.11. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee note that the Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan (PM 
VIKAS) Scheme created by merging various Schemes i.e., Seekho aur Kamao, 
USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil was allocated ₹540.00 
crore in 2023-24. The Committee also note that under PM VIKAS Committed 
Liabilities head, Actual Expenditure was ₹209.42 crore out of Revised Estimates 
of ₹215.98 crore in 2023-24. The Committee further note that under PM VIKAS 
Scheme head, for the year 2023-24 the Revised Expenditure was ₹109.88 crore 
and no expenditure could be made as the scheme did not initiate. Since the 
Scheme is approved till 2025-26, the Committee believe that the Ministry of 
Minority affairs will make efforts to ensure that the benefits reaped from the 
erstwhile Schemes by the poor section of the minority communities would 
continue. The Committee recommend that the Department should take steps 
to remove all the hurdles in implementation of the Scheme so that BE for the 
year 2024-25 would be utilized fully. The committee would like to be informed 
in this regard.” 
 
1.12. The Ministry of Minority Affairs, in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as 
under:- 
 “The observation of the Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance.” 
 
1.13. In their original Report, the Committee noted that the several 
schemes such as Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, 
and Nai Manzil have been merged into a single scheme i.e., Pradhan Mantri 
Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) but no expenditure was incurred under 
the Scheme in the year 2023-24. The Committee had, accordingly, 
recommended the Ministry of Minority Affairs to take steps to remove all 
the hurdles in implementation of the Scheme so that BE for the year 2024-
25 is fully utilized as the 15th Finance Commission cycle will come to an end 
by 2025-26.  The Committee are not satisfied with the routine reply of the 
Ministry that they have noted the observations of the Committee for 
compliance. The Committee expected a more comprehensive reply, clearly 
outlining the concrete steps taken to ensure full utilization of Budget 
allocation in 2024-25 under the scheme.  Hence, the Committee desire that 

7 
 
the Ministry should make sincere efforts to address the issues hindering 
expenditure and ensure timely approval of viable projects/proposals under 
all the four components of PM-VIKAS Scheme so that the allocated funds 
are fully utilized.  The Committee would like the Ministry to apprise them 
about the steps taken in this regard at Final Action Taken stage. 
 
 
  

8 
 
 
CHAPTER-II 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation (Para No. 2.9) 
The Committee note that ₹2,064.95 crore were surrendered by the Ministry of Minority 
Affairs out of Budgetary Allocation of ₹3,094.60 crore in 2023-24. The Committee find 
that the major reasons for surrendering of funds are revalidation of applications under 
Pre-Matric, Post-Matric and Merit cum means Scholarship Schemes, discontinuation of 
some Schemes, less / non-receipt of proposals from State/ UT Governments. The 
Committee feel that the responsibility of implementation of the Schemes since lies 
with the States/ UT Governments, they should timely complete all the procedural 
formalities on their part so that the Ministry of Minority Affairs is able to release funds. 
The Committee are of the view that the Ministry of Minority Affairs should develop a 
mechanism to guide the various implementing agencies so that a delay by State/UT 
Governments is avoided and may also examine incorporating a penal provision against 
the State/ UT Governments in case the response from the State/ UT Governments is 
not received in a stipulated time period 
Reply of the Government 
Ministry implements three scholarship schemes viz. Pre-Matric, Post Matric and Meritc-
m-Means for the educational empowerment of 6 centrally notified minority 
communities. Under these schemes, the scholarship amount is disbursed to the 
beneficiaries through Direct Benefits Transfer Mode under Aadhar Mode Biometric 
System while the administrative expenses release to States/UTs on reimbursement 
basis.  
As these schemes are yet to be approved for implementation beyond 2021-22 neither 
any target fixed nor scheme could be implemented from 2022-23 onwards. This 
Ministry endeavours to get these schemes approved for implementation beyond 2021-
22 after harmonization with similar schemes of other Central Ministries, with approval 
of the Competent Authority in the Government at the earliest. 
(Ministry of Minority Affairs    OM No. G-20014/1/2025- Budget    Dated      
19.03.2025) 
Recommendation (Para No. 4.13) 
The Committee appreciate the efforts made by the Ministry of Minority Affairs by 
developing community infrastructure and basic amenities in the identified areas for 
improving the quality of life of the minority community under Multi-Sectoral 
Development Scheme. The Committee believe that the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas 
Karyakram (PMJVK) introduced in 2017-18 to replace Multi-Sectoral Development 
Scheme has great potential to further improve the quality of life as it would cover the 
entire country including aspirational districts. The Committee note that the allocation 

9 
 
to the Ministry of Minority Affairs under this head has considerably gone down in 
comparison to the allocation made in 2021-22 and 2022-23. The Committee feel that 
since all the districts in the Country are covered under the Scheme, the allocation 
should have been enhanced. There is no doubt that the State/UT Government plays 
an important role as they have been entrusted the responsibility of implementing the 
Scheme, however, the Ministry of Minority Affairs cannot absolve themselves from the 
responsibility to successfully implement the Scheme hence State/UT Governments 
should have been regularly pursued to follow the PFMS and SNA guidelines. The 
Committee are happy to find that the PFMS and SNA guidelines have now been 
adopted by most of the States and UTs but would like the Ministry to ensure that the 
remaining States/UTs also comply to the PFMS and SNA guidelines without any delay. 
In order to stop recurrence of such issues the Ministry of Minority Affairs may review 
them on regular basis. 
Reply of the Government 
 
The observations of Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance. The 
frequency of review meetings regarding implementation of PMJVK, timely completion 
of approved projects, adherence to the PFMS and SNA guidelines have been increased. 
States/UTs are being instructed and helped for the specific’s issues being faced by 
them for completion and execution of approved projects. 
  
Presently the expenditure status as Rs. 641.41 crore against the RE of Rs. 908.90 
crore as on 31.01.2025 is satisfactory.  During the financial year 2025-26, the budget 
estimates   for implementation of PMJVK scheme is    an amount of Rs. 1913.97 crore. 
  
(Ministry of Minority Affairs OM No. G-20014/1/2025- Budget Dated    
19.03.2025) 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 4.14) 
The Committee note that 809296 Projects have been completed and 115811 Projects 
are in progress under Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK). The Committee 
find that 145981 projects have been dropped due to various reasons but not due to 
non-receipt/availability of funds from State/UT Governments. The most prevalent 
reasons for dropping the Projects is due to the non-availability of land for the Project 
and inordinate delay on part of the respective States/UTs. The Committee find that 
the Ministry of Minority Affairs would ensure that the funds are released for newly 
Projects only after completion of due tendering process and award of works and have 
also advised the State/UT Governments to utilize the unspent balance in SNA Account 
for completion of ongoing Projects before asking for fresh funds and reconcile the 
account with the Central Government. The Committee also find that hew Projects 
would be approved only after review of performance regarding execution of earlier 
approved Projects to the concerned State/UTs/CGO. The Committee hope that the 
steps taken by the Ministry would yield the desired results and the Ministry, in future, 
may not face any difficulty in execution of the Projects approved by them. Since large 

10 
 
number of Projects sanctioned to States/CGOs are under execution, the Committee 
would like the Ministry to lay down the time limit for completion of these Projects so 
that they are not inordinately delayed as delay increases the cost and also causes the 
inconvenience to the beneficiaries. Further, the Committee are sure that a mobile app 
PMJVK Bhuvan developed by the Ministry would help in keeping check on the progress 
of the Projects under execution, however, Committee desire that the Ministry will 
ensure that all the State/UT Governments will take necessary steps to geo-tag all such 
Projects a time bound manner and the Ministry may caution the State/UT 
Governments in case of any irregularity or delay observed. The Committee strongly 
believe that the infrastructure and basic amenities created under the scheme are 
crucial for improving the quality of life of the people belonging to Minority communities 
and the Projects dropped must have been a great service for them. The Committee 
desire that these dropped projects may be revisited with a view to revive them and 
the necessary steps may be taken by the Ministry of Minority Affairs to address the 
hindrances execution of such Projects. The Committee would like to be apprised in 
this regard. 
Reply of the Government 
Most of the observation of Hon’ble committee are already being implemented 
by the Ministry.  Further, the Ministry from time-to-time issues instructions to the 
States /UTs/ CGOs for timely execution and completion of the projects keeping in view 
the principle of time overrun means cost overrun. During the review meeting taken at 
the level of Joint Secretary in December, 2024 and again at the level of the Secretary 
(Minority Affairs) in January, 2025 all the State Govt. have been instructed to complete 
the projects units by the June 2025 which were sanctioned up to the year 2020-21. A 
National Review Meeting held on 11.03.2025 under the Chairmanship of Secretary 
(MA), with representatives from the State/UT Governments and CGOs to review and 
evaluate the performance of States/UTs/CGOs in execution of PMJVK. 
  
As regard the dropped projects, this is to state that all the units have been 
dropped after due consultations and as requested by the concerned State Govts. /U.T. 
Administrations / CGOs only. 
(Ministry of Minority Affairs OM No. G-20014/1/2025- Budget    
19.03.2025) 
Recommendation (Para No. 5.8) 
 
Keeping the importance of skill development for the financial independence and 
growth of the poor people in the country, the Committee strongly feel that the 
erstwhile Schemes of skill development of the Ministry of Minority Affairs viz., Seekho 
aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil may have served 
the purpose for poor people in the Minority Communities. The Committee note that 
large number of people from the Minority Communities benefitted from these Schemes 

11 
 
during 2018-19 to 2022-23. However, these Schemes are not in operation since 2023-
24. The Committee are of the view that any move of the Government to dilute them 
would adversely affect the economic empowerment of the Minority Communities. The 
Committee find that the Ministry of Minority Affairs have spent ₹ 209.42 crore on the 
committed liability after merger of all these Schemes into a single scheme called 
Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS). The Committee hope that the 
Ministry of Minority Affairs will continue funding the committed liability for the required 
period so that beneficiaries undergoing training continue to get training. The 
Committee would like to be informed of the number of persons currently undergoing 
training under the erstwhile Schemes and the time by which their training would be 
completed. 
Reply of the Government  
PM VIKAS is an umbrella scheme converging five erstwhile scheme of the 
Ministry namely-Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshani and Nai 
Manzil. PM VIKAS scheme has the following components namely: 
I  Component   1: - Skilling and Training 
II Component   2:- Woman Leadership and Entrepreneurship 
III  Component  3:- Education(through NIOS) 
IV Component   4:- Infrastructure Development

OF THE GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED AND WHICH REQUIRE

Recommendation (Para No. 2.8) 
The Committee note that the delay in adoption of procedural changes introduced by 
the Ministry of Finance such as SNA system, PFMS by the State/UT Governments 
resulted in under-utilisation of Budgetary/ Revised Estimates in 2023-24 and 2023-24. 
The Committee firmly believe that with these procedural changes the financial 
resources of the Government of India will not get stuck up in the State treasury and 
can be fruitfully utilised by the Ministry of Minority Affairs on other welfare measures. 
Since the State/UT Governments have streamlined the system by adopting the 
procedural changes, the Committee expect that the Ministry of Minority Affairs would 
be able to spend their budgetary allocation for 2024-25 on the various schemes for 
the welfare of minority communities. The Committee are, however, apprehensive as 
they feel that the actual expenditure in 2024-25 may again be less than the Budgetary 
Estimates as the approval of several Schemes of Ministry of Minority Affairs is at 
various stages. The Committee, therefore desire that the approval of the Schemes of 
the Ministry of Minority Affairs should be expedited so that Schemes such as 
Scholarship Schemes and PM-VIKAS are implemented without any delay, thus avoiding 
under-utilisation of Budgetary Estimates. In view of the above, the Committee, 
recommend that the necessary mechanism may be evolved so that the Schemes 
requiring approval is timely obtained so that the benefit of the Schemes reaches the 
deprived sections of the Minority Communities. 
Reply of the Government 
The Observations of Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance.  
 
PMJVK: 
The Ministry has taken pro-active steps to utilise BE allocations in r/o PMJVK 
Scheme. The expenditure till 31.01.2025 under the scheme is ₹641.41 crore against 
the RE of ₹908.90 crore. Furthermore, additional amount of ₹100 crore have been 
requested for in the 2nd batch of supplementary for F.Y. 2024-25 and it is assured that 
the fund will be utilised fully. 
 
Scholarship: 
Ministry implements three scholarship schemes viz. Pre-Matric, Post Matric and 
Meritc-cum-Means for the educational empowerment of 6 centrally notified minority 
communities. Under these schemes, the scholarship amount is disbursed to the 
beneficiaries through Direct Benefits Transfer Mode under Aadhar Mode Biometric 
System while the administrative expenses release to States/UTs on reimbursement 

14 
 
basis. Hence the SNA system is not applicable in case of 3 scholarship schemes for 
minorities.  
As these schemes are yet to be approved for implementation beyond 2021-22 
neither any target fixed nor scheme could be implemented from 2022-23 onwards. 
This Ministry endeavours to get these schemes approved for implementation beyond 
2021-22 after harmonization with similar schemes of other Central Ministries, with 
approval of the Competent Authority in the Government at the earliest. 
PM VIKAS: 
Ministry has expedited the roll out of PM VIKAS scheme. Approval of the 
competent authority has already been obtained on the scheme of the guidelines of 
the PM VIKAS Scheme. The Ministry has started the receiving proposals from the 
eligible organisation under the scheme. Meeting of Screening Committee was held on 
12th February,2025 to examine and discuss the proposals. The meeting of the 
Empowered Committee under the Chairmanship of Secretary MoMA was held on 10th 
March,2025. On ground project implementation is expected to start in April,2025. 
(Ministry of Minority Affairs  OM No. G-20014/1/2025- Budget    Dated    
19.03.2025) 
Recommendation (Para No. 3.16) 
The Committee find that the Ministry of Minority Affairs implements Pre-Matric 
Scholarship Scheme, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme, Merit cum means based 
scholarship, Maulana Azad National Fellowship and Padho Pradesh Scheme for the 
educational empowerment of minority communities. The Committee, however, find 
that the Maulana Azad National Fellowship and Padho Pardesh Scheme have been 
discontinued with effect from 2022-23 and the remaining educational empowerment 
Schemes viz. Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme, Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme are 
pending for approval since 2021-22. The Committee are of the view that education of 
the students belonging to minority communities should not be made to suffer for the 
administrative delays and necessary measures should be taken to ensure that there is 
no interruption in implementation of the Schemes. Since, the process of harmonisation 
of Scholarship Schemes of all the Ministries/ Departments is in progress, the 
Committee desire this exercise should be expedited. The Committee are aware that 
several other educational empowerment Schemes such as National Fellowship, 
National Overseas Scholarship, Free Coaching, Residential education, etc. are being 
implemented for the educational empowerment of various marginalised sections of 
the society by various Ministries/Departments. The Committee would, therefore, like 
the Ministry of Minority Affairs to examine the need of implementing other educational 
empowering schemes for the poor students of minority communities so that they may 
also avail the best of education and contribute in the growth of the nation. The 
Committee would also like to recommend that the Scholarship Schemes pending for 
approval should be approved without further delay. 
 

15

Ministry implements three scholarship schemes viz. Pre-Matric, Post Matric and Meritc-
m-Means for the educational empowerment of 6 centrally notified minority 
communities. As these schemes are yet to be approved for implementation beyond 
2021-22 neither any target fixed nor scheme could be implemented from 2022-23 
onwards. This Ministry endeavours to get these schemes approved for implementation 
beyond 2021-22 after harmonization with similar schemes of other Central Ministries, 
with approval of the Competent Authority in the Government at the earliest. 
 
(Ministry of Minority Affairs OM No. G-20014/1/2025- Budget Dated 
19.03.2025) 
Recommendation (Para No. 5.9) 
The Committee note that the Pradhan Mantri Virasat ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) 
Scheme created by merging various Schemes i.e., Seekho aur Kamao, USTTAD, 
Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil was allocated ₹540.00 crore in 2023-24. 
The Committee also note that under PM VIKAS Committed Liabilities head, Actual 
Expenditure was ₹209.42 crore out of Revised Estimates of ₹215.98 crore in 2023-24. 
The Committee further note that under PM VIKAS Scheme head, for the year 2023-24 
the Revised Expenditure was ₹109.88 crore and no expenditure could be made as the 
scheme did not initiate. Since the Scheme is approved till 2025-26, the Committee 
believe that the Ministry of Minority affairs will make efforts to ensure that the benefits 
reaped from the erstwhile Schemes by the poor section of the minority communities 
would continue. The Committee recommend that the Department should take steps 
to remove all the hurdles in implementation of the Scheme so that BE for the year 
2024-25 would be utilized fully. The committee would like to be informed in this 
regard. 
Reply of the Government 
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance. 
(Ministry of Minority Affairs OM No. G-20014/1/2025- Budget Dated   
19.03.2025)

CHAPTER-V 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE 
GOVERNMENT ARE INTERIM IN NATURE 
(Recommendation Para No.2.10) 
The Committee note that the Schemes of the Ministry of Minority Affairs are now broadly 
classified into three categories viz. (i) Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram, (ii) Educational 
Empowerment initiatives; and (iii) Skilling and livelihood initiatives. The Committee believe 
that these Schemes are ray of hope for the poor people of Minority Communities and their 
welfare can be carried out with the sincere and effective implementation of the Schemes 
falling under each of the component. The Committee find that in many of the Schemes no 
physical targets were fixed. Since the welfare measures are meant for poor people of the 
minority communities, it becomes necessary that the physical targets are fixed annually to 
assess the success of the Scheme and also to find the percentage of population of minority 
community benefitted from these Schemes. Further, this would also help in appropriate 
allocation of funds under each Scheme at the beginning of the financial year. The Committee, 
therefore, recommend that the Ministry of Minority Affairs may examine the viability of fixing 
targets under each Scheme and develop a suitable system to annually fix the physical targets 
under various Schemes that have a quantifiable outcome. 
Reply of the Government 
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee has been noted for compliance. 
As regards, Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) required targets are fixed 
on the OOMF (Output Outcome Monitoring Framework) of the NITI Aayog.  Regular quarterly, 
half-yearly and annual reviews are done not only at the Ministry’s level but at the level of NITI 
Aayog. Ministry implements three scholarship schemes viz. Pre-Matric, Post Matric and Meritc-
m-Means for the educational empowerment of 6 centrally notified minority communities. 
Under these schemes, the scholarship amount is disbursed to the beneficiaries through Direct 
Benefits Transfer Mode under Aadhar Mode Biometric System while the administrative 
expenses release to States/UTs on reimbursement basis.  
As these schemes are yet to be approved for implementation beyond 2021-22 neither 
any target fixed nor scheme could be implemented from 2022-23 onwards. This Ministry 
endeavours to get these schemes approved for implementation beyond 2021-22 after 
harmonization with similar schemes of other Central Ministries, with approval of the 
Competent Authority in the Government at the earliest.

Government in respect of all the observations/recommendations have been examined

1.4. The Committee will now deal with the replies received from the Government 
which need reiteration or merit comments. 
 
A.  SCHOLARSHIP FOR HIGHER EDUCATION FOR YOUNG ACHIEVERS 
SCHEME (SHREYAS) FOR SCs 
     
   Recommendation (Para No.4.28) 
1.5. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Scholarship for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS) 
for SCs is the Umbrella Scheme which has four existing sub-Schemes viz. 
National Fellowships for SCs, National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for SCs, 
Top Class Education Scheme for SCs and Free Coaching Scheme for SC and 
OBC students. The Committee note that the budgetary allocation for 2022-23 
and 2023-24 was less in comparison to 2021-22 but the actual expenditure has 
been constantly increasing since 2021-22, as it was ₹271.21 crore, ₹293.77 
crore and ₹363.31crore in 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24, respectively. The 
Committee find that the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs and OBC is not available 
on the National Scholarship Portal and onboarding of the Scheme on the portal 
is under consideration. The Committee also find that the Scheme is being 
implemented by Dr Ambedkar Foundation through empanelled Central 
Universities after revision of the Scheme in 2023-24 and only 19 Central 
Universities have signed the MOU with the Foundation. The Committee desire 
that the Department should take necessary steps to on-board the Free 
Coaching Scheme for SCs and OBCs on National Scholarship Portal and more 
Central Universities should be empanelled so that a large number of students 
of SC and OBC communities are able to appear in competitive and entrance 
examinations for obtaining jobs in Public/Private Sector as well as to secure 
admission in reputed higher educational institutions.” 
 
1.6. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment), in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as under:- 
“Continuous follow-up is done with all 56 Central Universities. However, as on 
date, only 19 Central Universities have signed Memorandum of Understanding 
(MoU) with Dr. Ambedkar Foundation and become part of the Scheme. The 
Department will continue its efforts for on-boarding more Central Universities.”  
 
 
 

3 
 
 
1.7.  The Committee, while acknowledging the steady increase in the 
actual expenditure over the last three years under the Scholarship for 
Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS), had observed 
that the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs and OBCs is not available on the 
National Scholarship Portal. Following the revision of SHREYAS Scheme in 
2023-24, the Committee found that the Scheme is being implemented by 
Dr. Ambedkar Foundation through empanelled Central Universities and 19 
Central Universities have signed the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) 
with the Foundation. The Ministry have informed that while continuous 
follow-up is being done with all 56 Central Universities, only 19 Central 
Universities have signed MoU with Dr. Ambedkar Foundation so far. In order 
to enhance the effectiveness and reach of the SHREYAS scheme aimed at 
benefiting a larger number of students from SC and OBC communities, the 
Committee reiterate that the Department should expedite the process of 
on-boarding the Free Coaching Scheme for SCs and OBCs on the National 
Scholarship Portal. Further, the Committee desire that the Department 
should strive to empanel remaining Central Universities with the Ambedkar 
Foundation as early as possible, thereby, expanding its reach to enable 
large number of students preparing for competitive examinations and 
securing admission in reputed higher educational institutions can take 
advantage of the Scheme. 
 
B.  PRADHAN MANTRI ANUSUCHIT JAATI ABHYUDAY YOJANA (PM-
AJAY) 
    Recommendation (Para No.5.9) 
1.8. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee note that Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana 
(PM-AJAY) is an Umbrella scheme wherein 3 centrally sponsored scheme, 
namely, Pradhan Mantri Adrash Gram Yojana (PM-AJAY), Special Central 
Assistance to Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SCA to SCSP) and Babu Jagjivan Ram 
Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY) have been merged in 2021-22 due to similarity in 
nature. The Committee find that since 2021-22, 6282 villages in the country 
have been declared Adrash Grams, Rs.1023 crore provided to 184815 

4 
 
beneficiaries under GIA component and Rs. 114.23 crore sanctioned for 44 
hostels covering 4985 beneficiaries. The Committee appreciate the efforts of 
the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment for taking several steps for 
effective implementation of the Scheme. The Committee are however, slightly 
worried with the pace of actual expenditure incurred during 2022-23 and 2023-
24. The Committee feel that the gap between Budgetary Estimate and Actual 
Expenditure should be narrowed down so that the objectives of the Scheme are 
fully achieved. The State Governments should be guided to take necessary 
steps so that more and more villages are declared Adarsh Grams in their States 
as it has happened in Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Madhya Pradesh. Similarly, 
the construction of hostels in educational institutions should also be prioritized 
as large numbers of students belonging to SC community are not able to join 
good educational institution due to limited availability of hostels.” 
 
1.9. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment), in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as under:- 
 
“The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY), consists of 
three components namely Adarsh Gram, Grants in Aid to State/District level 
Projects and Hostel component. The scheme is 100 % centrally sponsored and 
being implemented by the State Government/UT Administration. The 
expenditure incurred during last two years has been relatively low due to the 
introduction of the SNA system which requires States/UTs to complete the 
necessary mapping, causing a procedural delay. Additionally, pending 
Utilization Certificates and fewer proposals for Hostels and non-submission of 
Grants-in-aid perspective plans by some States contributed to reduced 
expenditure. To address this, the Department holds monthly review meetings 
and maintains regular communication with States/UTs to improve 
implementation, clear SNA balances, and ensure timely submission of UCs for 
smooth fund release. Furthermore, Ministry officials visit villages to oversee the 
implementation of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyudyay Yojana (PM-
AJAY) so that declaration of Adarsh Gram is expedited by the State 
Governments. This Department is implementing Hostel component of PM-AJAY 
which aims to increase literacy and encourage enrolment of SCs students in 
schools and higher educational institutions by providing adequate residential 
facilities in quality institutions, especially in the SC dominated blocks and 
elsewhere in India.  
With efforts and follow-up, as compared to earlier years during the FY 2024-
25, the utilisation was Rs 736 Crore as against Rs 471 Crore in FY 2023-24 
which is an increase of 56%. The Department will ensure higher utilisation in 
the next financial year.” 

5 
 
 
1.10.  While appreciating the efforts taken by the Department for effective 
implementation of PM-AJAY Scheme, the Committee highlighted the need 
for narrowing the gap between the Budgetary Estimates and the Actual 
Expenditure under the Scheme. The Committee further opined the need for 
guiding the State Governments towards more villages being declared 
Adarsh Grams and to prioritize the construction of hostels in educational 
institutions. The Department have informed that low expenditure in the last 
two years were due to introduction of the SNA system, pending Utilization 
Certificates, fewer proposal for Hostels and non-submission of Grants-in-
aid perspective plans by some States. On the implementation of the hostel 
component of PM-AJAY, the Department have informed that they are 
providing adequate residential facilities in quality institutions, especially in

should take necessary measures to ensure that the reasons affecting 
utilization of funds do not anymore hinder the expenditure and improve 
further to maximise utilization of funds. Further, in order to ensure timely 
implementation and maximum benefit to SC communities, the Committee 
reiterate the need for prioritizing the construction of hostels in educational

Government of India has taken several measures such as enactment of 
Protection of Civil Rights (PCR) Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and 
Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. The Committee note that 
a centrally sponsored scheme was introduced to financially assist the 
States/UTs for strengthening the machinery for Implementation of these Acts. 

6

States have not been able to set up the requisite system to effectively 
implement the provisions contained in the Acts and to deal with the cases of

requirement as per the provisions made in the Acts, has been made a

   Recommendation (Para No.9.22)

of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Department of Drinking Water & 
Sanitation and Ministry of skill Development and Entrepreneurship. As per the 
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, there are likely to be one lakh Sewer and 
Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) in the country. The Ministry of Housing and Urban 
Affairs are required to converge for interventions such as profiling of SSWs 
through MIS portal, nomination of Responsible Sanitation Authority, setting up 
of Emergency Response Sanitation Unit, etc. In view of the involvement of 
several Ministries/ Departments/ Organisations, the Committee are of the 
opinion that for the success of the NAMASTE, it is important that there is proper 
coordination amongst them so that the responsibilities entrusted over them are 
carried out smoothly. Unless all the SSWs are validated, they would be deprived 
from the benefits of the Scheme. The Committee find that out of 43961 profiled 
SSWs, 37407 SSWs have been validated by the concerned Urban Local Bodies. 
The Committee, therefore, desire that all the SSWs should be profiled and 
validated urgently. Further, the pace of the distribution of PPE Kits, Safety 
devices and Ayushman Bharat Cards to SSWs is required to be increased as 
only 16741 PPE Kits, 42 Safety Devices and 13412 Ayushman Bharat Cards

Social Justice and Empowerment would take all necessary steps for the welfare 
of the SSWs and effective Implementation of NAMASTE in a time bound 
manner.”

States/UTs. Profiling has been carried out in all States / UTs.  Tamil Nadu and

SSWs by Tamil Nadu and Odisha will be merged with details of validated SSWs.

11

Recommendation (Para No.2.12) 
The Committee find that the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment have 
fixed annual physical targets for various schemes such as Pre-Matric and Post-Matric 
Scholarship Schemes, National Fellowships for SCs, National Oversees Scholarships 
for SCs, Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Samparna Hitgrahi (PM- DAKSH) etc. 
Simultaneously, the Committee also find that there are several schemes under which 
physical targets are not fixed by the Department, such as Pradhan Mantri Adarsh 
Gram Yojana (PMAGY), Babu Jagjiwan Ram Chatrawas Yojana (BJRCY) and Venture 
Capital Fund (VCF) for SCs and OBCs, etc. The Committee believe that the success 
of any scheme can be measured with the achievement of targets/ goals. In the 
absence of targets/goals it would not be possible to assess the outcome of any 
scheme. The Committee would be happy if the annual physical targets are fixed for 
such Schemes where the welfare measures can be quantified as the Committee have 
found that the schemes with targets perform better than the Scheme without annual 
targets. In view of the above, the Committee would like the Department of Social 
Justice and Empowerment to examine the viability and fix the physical targets of all 
the welfare schemes of the Department so that there is no laxity in the 
implementation of the Schemes at any stage by the States or other Implementing 
Agencies. 
Reply of the Government 
In so far as Pre-Matric & Post-Matric Scholarship schemes for SCs are concerned no 
annual targets are fixed by the DoSJE.  The scheme is a saturation-based scheme and 
whosoever applies and is eligible is sanctioned the scholarship irrespective of the 
number of students.  As regards National Fellowships and National Overseas 
Scholarships for SCs annual maximum slots are fixed.   
Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana (PMAGY) is one component of umbrella scheme 
PM-AJAY.  Under this component infrastructure development in identified SC Villages 
are being covered.  Since the thrust is on gap-filling of infrastructure in the identified 

13 
 
villages, the targets related to beneficiaries cannot be computed and predicted. 
However, there is an overall target of number of villages to be declared as Adarsh 
Gram.The VCF-SC (including ASIIM) and VCF-BC specify year-wise targets for the 
number of SC and BC-owned companies to be supported through assistance under 
these schemes until the closure of the fund.  Under VCF-SC, an annual target of 
supporting 18 companies and nurturing 250 new incubation ideas and startups has 
been set.  Under VCF-BC, the annual target is to support 13 companies owned by 
entrepreneurship from Backward Classes.  The Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana 
(BJRCY) is now amalgamated into Hostel Component of PM-AJAY wherein, proposals 
are received from the State Governments/UTs after conducting a need based study 
for the requirement of hostel for SC students.  As this component of the scheme is 
based on proposals received from States, the targets are not fixed. However, under 
this Scheme a certain percentage of funds are allocated for the Hostel Component of 
PM-AJAY Scheme.

CHAPTER - I 
REPORT 
 
The Report deals with the action taken by the Government on the 
Observations/Recommendations of the Committee contained in their Sixth Report 
(Eighteenth Lok Sabha) on ‘Demands for Grants (2025-26)’ of the Department of 
Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (Ministry of Social Justice and 
Empowerment).  
 
1.2. The Sixth Report was presented to Lok Sabha and laid in Rajya Sabha on 
17.03.2025. It contained 27 observations/recommendations. Action Taken Replies of 
Government in respect of all the observations/recommendations have been examined 
and are categorized as under: - 
(i) Observations/Recommendations which have 
been accepted by the Government: - Rec. Para

2 
 
  
1.3. The Committee desire that action taken notes on the recommendations 
contained in Chapter-I and final action taken notes in respect of the 
recommendations contained in Chapter-V of this Report may be furnished to 
them at the earliest and in any case not later than three months of the 
presentation of this Report.  
 
1.4. The Committee will now deal with the replies received from the Government which 
need reiteration or merit comments. 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 2.15) 
  
1.5. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“From a thorough examination of the Demands for Grants (DFG) over the past 
three years, the Committee observe a persistent trend of underutilization of 
funds across key schemes such as ADIP, SIPDA, DDRS, and Scholarships, with 
actual expenditures consistently falling short of Revised Estimates (RE) and 
Budget Estimates (BE). The BE allocations were invariably reduced at the RE 
stage in 2022-23, 2023-24, and 2024-25, yet the Department was unable to fully 
utilize even the reduced funds. The Department utilized 97.38 per cent of RE in 
2022-23 and 93.39 per cent in 2023-24. However, as of 03.03.2025, only 
₹892.68 crore of ₹1,167.27 crore (76.48 per cent) has been spent. This shortfall 
was primarily due to disruptions from the introduction of the CNA and TSA 
models. Delays in receiving Utilization Certificates (UCs) from State Governments 
under SIPDA and a lack of adequate proposals from North-Eastern States further 
hindered funds utilization. While the Committee were assured by the 
Department’s representatives that the remaining 2024-25 funds would be fully 
utilized by 31.03.2025, the Committee strongly urge the Department to adopt 
targeted remedial measures and strategic interventions to ensure efficient fund 
utilization in 2025-26. Proactive engagement with State Governments, NGOs, 

3 
 
and implementing agencies is essential to streamline proposal submissions and 
disbursement process, particularly for skill training programs and capital 
expenditure. Furthermore, given the challenges in meeting fixed targets for 
schemes like SIPDA and DDRS, the Department should reassess target-setting 
methodologies to ensure that they are realistic, flexible, and aligned with 
performance trends. The Committee recommend decisive action to improve fund 
utilization and program execution in the remaining year of the 2024-26 financial 
cycle, ensuring that allocated resources effectively advance the welfare of 
persons with disabilities and that the Department successfully meets its 
commitments under various schemes.” 
  
1.6. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment 
of Persons with Disabilities), in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as under:-  
 “The suggestions of the Committee has been noted. 
In FY 2024-25, the Department has spent ₹1,112.61 crore against the RE of 
₹1,167.27 crore i.e. 95.32 % of RE allocation. Further, it is also mentioned that 
approximately ₹47 crore has been returned to CFI from TSA account as various 
State Governments/Implementing agencies/NGOs/organizations etc have not 
withdrawn funds by 31.03.2025.  The Scheme wise details are given below: 
  
ADIP Scheme: For FY 2024-25, against the RE of ₹350.00 crores, amount of 
₹348.81 crores has been spent. The balance amount of ₹1.19 crores was 
surrendered under the media head due to non-withdrawal of funds by 
Directorate of Advertisement and Visual Publicity (DAVP) for expenditure incurred 
by them under ADIP Scheme. Under the ADIP Scheme, BE for FY 2025-26 is        
₹316.70 crores that will be utilized in various activities under ADIP Scheme. For 
FY 2025-26, sufficient demand for funds has been raised by ALIMCO which is the 
major Implementing Agency of ADIP Scheme. Apart from this, demand for funds 
has also been raised by National Institutes for pilot projects on teaching/learning 
materials (TLM) Kits. 

4 
 
  
SIPDA Scheme: Under SIPDA Scheme, during 2024-25, an amount of ₹44.16 
crore has been spent out of RE of ₹111.00 crore, Further, due to implementation 
of TSA module from 2024-25, some States could not onboard on TSA module 
and make expenditure of sanctioned amount of about ₹ 40 crore. 
In order to address the shortfall in fund utilization and to facilitate full 
appropriate utilization of funds, the Department is actively pursuing several 
redressal mechanisms, such as: 
Screening Committee: 
  
A committee has been constituted of Joint Secretary (SIPDA), Director/Deputy 
Secretary (SIPDA), and two experts in the field of disability to duly examine the 
proposals for release of Grant-in-Aid (GIA) under the Barrier Free and Accessible 
India component. 
  
Strengthening Coordination with States and Implementing Agencies: 
The Department engages proactively with State Governments, particularly 
focusing on improving the timely submission of Utilization Certificates (UCs) and 
correct proposals. Periodic virtual and in-person review meetings are being held 
to track progress under SIPDA. 
  
Process Optimization Post-CNA and TSA Introduction: 
  
Recognizing the transitional disruptions caused by the adoption of the Central 
Nodal Agency (CNA) and Treasury Single Account (TSA) systems, the 
Department has streamlined fund release protocols and updated internal SOPs to 
minimize delays in disbursement and expenditure. 
  
DDRS Scheme: Under DDRS Scheme, an amount of ₹139.39 crore has been spent 
during the financial year 2024–25 as against the revised estimate of ₹139.00 crore. 

5 
 
Under the DDRS scheme, the following measures have been taken by this 
Department for smooth utilization of funds as under: 
a. Model projects have been conceptualized to cover all 21 disabilities as per RPwD 
Act, 2016. 
b. Maximum age limit of the ID beneficiaries has been increased from 18 to 23 
years. 
c. Grant-in-aid to the Implementing Agencies is being released on Advance-cum-
reimbursement basis. 
d. With effect from 2023-24, the implementing agencies are required to submit 
UDID cards of all the eligible beneficiaries. The data regarding UDID cards is 
being directly fetched through API from UDID Portal (Swavlamban Portal). 
e. With effect from 01.10.2024 the following procedure has been rolled out for 
expediting fund release: If the proposal submitted by the PIAs/NGOs on e-
anudaan portal is pending at District level for one month without any action, 
then it will automatically be forwarded to the State Government. Further, if the 
same proposal is pending with the State Government for one month without any 
action, then it will automatically be forwarded (without recommendation of State 
Government) to the Department. However, this will not be applicable in case of 
supplementary grant is being given by the State Government to the PIAs/NGOs. 
f. CPMU consultants and young professionals of the Department are conducting 
video inspections to monitor the smooth functioning of the organizations and the 
timely submission of grants-in-aid proposals. 
  
Scholarship Scheme: Under Scholarship Scheme, an amount of ₹89.71 crore has 
been spent during 2024-25 against the RE allocation of ₹80.00 crore. The 
Department is actively organizing meetings with State Nodal Officers (SNOs) to 
ensure effective implementation of the schemes. The Department is also taking 
necessary steps to sensitize the States/UTs to clear the pendency at various levels 
of the State Nodal Officers and other Stakeholders. The Department has published 
advertisements in leading Newspapers across the country twice to increase 

6 
 
awareness of these schemes amongst students and other stakeholders. All other 
types of media and social media platforms are also used for spreading awareness. 
The Chief Secretaries/Principal Secretaries of the States are also addressed to 
spread awareness of the schemes through various mediums of communication in 
their respective States/UTs. 
  
The Department reiterates its commitment to the efficient and impactful 
implementation of all its flagship schemes and assures the Committee of sustained 
efforts to maximize fund utilization, enhance delivery mechanisms, and fulfill its 
mandate for the welfare of persons with disabilities.” 
 
1.7. In their original recommendation, the Committee had flagged the 
persistent underutilization of funds across key schemes—namely ADIP, 
SIPDA, DDRS, and Scholarships—despite fixed allocations and physical 
targets under the EFC framework. The Committee had called for targeted 
interventions, better coordination with States, and reassessment of planning 
and implementation processes. However, the Committee are not satisfied 
with the Government’s reply. While the Department has claimed improved 
fund utilization in 2024–25, actual figures—especially under the SIPDA 
scheme—continue to reflect substantial shortfalls, with less than 40% of RE 
spent and significant funds returned due to procedural delays. This is a 
recurring pattern which is observed over the past three years. The 
Committee note that procedural reforms have been introduced, such as 
automated proposal forwarding and stakeholder outreach. However, these 
do not adequately address structural issues like weak inter-agency 
coordination, delayed approvals, and lack of region-specific planning. The 
Committee reiterate that a more data-driven, accountable, and flexible 
implementation framework is needed to ensure that available resources are 
fully leveraged in the remaining years of the financial cycle. 
  

7 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 3.20) 
1.8. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee recognize that the Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for 
Purchase/Fitting of Aids/Appliances (ADIP) Scheme is an important initiative 
aimed at enhancing mobility, independence, and economic empowerment of 
Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). The Committee note that fund allocation and 
utilization under ADIP have shown a steady increase, with actual expenditure 
surpassing initial Budget Estimates (BE) in multiple years. In 2022-23, the BE 
was ₹235.00 crore, which was revised to ₹230.00 crore, yet actual expenditure 
exceeded expectations at ₹242.29 crore. Similarly, in 2023-24, the BE of ₹245.00 
crore was significantly revised to ₹305.00 crore, with actual spending at ₹290.60 
crore. In 2024-25, the BE was further enhanced to ₹315.00 crore, and the 
Revised Estimate (RE) increased to ₹350.00 crore, with ₹346.27 crore utilized as 
of 03.03.2025. The Committee also note that increased financial allocations has 
been ably matched by the physical performance/targets set under the Scheme. 
In 2022-23 and 2023-24, the target was exceeded, benefiting 2.89 lakh and 3.15 
lakh beneficiaries, respectively. However, in 2024-25, only 2.10 lakh beneficiaries 
were assisted as of 14.02.2025, accounting for 67 per cent of the target of 3.15 
lakh beneficiaries. While the Department has cited the imposition of the Model 
Code of Conduct during General Elections and the transition to the TSA Model-I 
as reasons for the slower pace of the expenditure, the Committee urge the 
Department to learn from these experiences and establish contingency plans to 
ensure uninterrupted service delivery in the future. The Committee however 
express concern over the reduction of the physical targets for 2025-26 to 2.05 
lakh beneficiaries and recommend that the Department continuously assess 
demand trends and explore possibilities for expanding beneficiary coverage.” 
 
 

8 
 
1.9. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment 
of Persons with Disabilities), in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as under:- 
  
“It is to apprise the committee that the process of onboarding on TSA module 
has been streamlined and Grants-in-Aid to Implementing Agencies under ADIP 
Scheme is being released through TSA module smoothly for financial year 2025-
26. However, the physical targets for beneficiaries was fixed considering the 
budgetary allocation of ₹316.70 cr under the Scheme for financial year 2025-26 
vis-à-vis RE of ₹350 cr. in 2024-25. Another major reason for decrease in 
number of beneficiaries is that demand for high end devices including motorised 
and lithium battery operated tricycles is low in comparison to other low-cost 
devices. 
  
As regard to beneficiary coverage, regular camps are being organised on basis of 
requests received from VIPs/other dignitaries. Also, sufficient demand for aids 
and appliances are being raised at PMDKs.  Apart from this, the Department is 
also encouraging Implementing Agencies for distribution of aids and appliances 
through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR).”  
 
1.10. In their original recommendation, the Committee had acknowledged 
the positive financial and physical performance of the ADIP Scheme over the 
years but had expressed concern on the significant drop in beneficiary 
coverage during 2024–25, alongside the downward revision of physical 
targets for 2025–26. The Committee had urged the Department to draw plan 
of action based on their experiences gained from recent administrative and 
operational challenges and ensure that service delivery remains consistent 
and demand-driven. 
 
In this context, the Committee find the reply of the Department to be 
somewhat limited in its scope. While the reasons cited—such as reduced 

9 
 
budgetary allocation and variation in demand for higher-end assistive 
devices—may partly explain the decline, the reply does not sufficiently 
elaborate on steps being taken to assess unmet needs or proactively expand 
outreach. The Committee believe that a more detailed and data-backed 
explanation would have added clarity, especially given the scheme’s 
significance in empowering persons with disabilities. The Committee, 
therefore, reiterate that the Department must strengthen its planning and 
monitoring mechanisms to ensure targets remain aligned with field-level 
demand. They recommend that future beneficiary projections be based on 
more granular assessments of regional needs and device preferences. 
Additionally, greater synergy with CSR initiatives and increased involvement 
of local stakeholders may help broaden the scheme’s reach and improve 
delivery outcomes. 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 4.18) 
1.11. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee note that physical targets under DDRS have witnessed a 
downward revision since 2024-25, with the target reduced from 40,000 in 2023-
24 to 32,000 in 2024-25 and 2025-26. The Department has attributed this to the 
number of projects supported remaining largely the same over the years, with 
new proposals being considered only after the release of funds to organizations. 
The Committee emphasize that rehabilitation services for PwDs should not be 
constrained due to procedural delays in fund disbursal and recommend that the 
Department take proactive steps to expedite approvals for new projects. The 
Committee urge the Department to explore expanding the scope of DDRS to 
cover more PwDs by identifying underserved areas where rehabilitation services 
are limited or absent.” 
 

10 
 
 
 
1.12. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment 
of Persons with Disabilities), in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as under:- 
“The observation of the Committee has been noted for compliance. In response 
to the Committee's suggestion, under DDRS scheme, all the new proposals are 
considered after recommendations of Screening Committee of the Department. 
Under the scheme, screening committee gives preferences to States and Districts 
where Model Projects are either not in existence or not adequately represented. 
Committee considers the proposal based on infrastructure, beneficiaries and 
service providers. 
The Department is committed to taking proactive steps to expedite the approval 
process for new projects by identifying underserved areas where rehabilitation 
services are limited or unavailable. This will enable us to reach a larger number 
of PwDs and improve the overall impact of our programs, ensuring that delays 
do not affect the delivery of essential services and helping us meet our target of 
40,000 beneficiaries.” 
1.13. The Committee note that physical targets under DDRS have witnessed 
a downward revision since 2024-25, with the target reduced from 40,000 in 
2023-24 to 32,000 in 2024-25 and 2025-26. The Department has attributed 
this to the number of projects supported remaining largely the same over the 
years, with new proposals being considered only after the release of funds to 
organizations. The Committee emphasised that rehabilitation services for 
PwDs should not be constrained due to procedural delays in fund disbursal 
and recommend that the Department take proactive steps to expedite 
approvals for new projects. The Committee urged the Department to explore 
expanding the scope of DDRS to cover more PwDs by identifying underserved 
areas where rehabilitation services are limited or absent. 

11 
 
The Committee appreciate the Department’s efforts in introducing 
monitoring mechanisms, including video inspections of NGOs and time-bound 
forwarding of proposals under the revised DDRS. The provision for automatic 
transmission of pending proposals from the district levels to the State 
Government and further to the DEPwD if no action is taken within a month of 
submission is a commendable measure aimed to streamline the approval 
process and minimize administrative delays. However, the Committee 
recommend strict enforcement of these provisions to ensure that no proposal 
remains pending for an unreasonable duration. Further, the Committee 
support the decision that organizations running both DDRS and National 
Trust schemes should choose only one to avoid duplication of services, 
ensuring that funds reach the maximum number of beneficiaries. 
 
 Recommendation (Para No. 5.15) 
1.14. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
 
“The Committee also find that persistent challenges such as delays in fund 
disbursement, pending utilization certificates, and incomplete proposals have 
impacted the effective implementation of SIPDA. Given that SIPDA is the flagship 
scheme for PwDs, the Committee strongly recommend that the Department 
strengthen its monitoring and coordination mechanisms by ensuring regular 
follow-ups with State Governments and implementing agencies. The Central 
Project Monitoring Unit (CPMU) should be further empowered to enable realtime 
tracking of fund utilization, proposal approvals, and physical progress under 
various sub-schemes. Furthermore, timely clearance of compliance documents 
such as Utilization Certificates (UCs) and pending proposals should be ensured to 
prevent underutilization and last-minute fund surrender.” 
 
 

12 
 
1.15. The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Empowerment  
 of Persons with Disabilities), in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as 
under:- 
“In order to address the shortfalls in fund utilization and to facilitate full 
appropriate utilization of funds, the Department is actively pursuing several 
redressal mechanism, such as: 
Screening Committee: 
  
A committee consisting of Joint Secretary (SIPDA), Director/Deputy Secretary 
(SIPDA), and two experts in the field of disability duly examine the proposals for 
release of Grant-in-Aid (GIA) under the Barrier Free and Accessible India 
component.

(Recommendation Para No.2.15) 
From a thorough examination of the Demands for Grants (DFG) over the past three 
years, the Committee observe a persistent trend of underutilization of funds across key 
schemes such as ADIP, SIPDA, DDRS, and Scholarships, with actual expenditures 
consistently falling short of Revised Estimates (RE) and Budget Estimates (BE). The BE 
allocations were invariably reduced at the RE stage in 2022-23, 2023- 24, and 2024-25, 
yet the Department was unable to fully utilize even the reduced funds. The Department 
utilized 97.38per cent of RE in 2022-23 and 93.39per cent in 2023-24. However, as of 
03.03.2025, only ₹892.68 crore of ₹ 1167.27 crore (76.48per cent) has been spent. 
This shortfall was primarily due to disruptions from the introduction of the CNA and TSA 
models. Delays in receiving Utilization Certificates (UCs) from State Governments under 
SIPDA and a lack of adequate proposals from North-Eastern States further hindered 
funds utilization. While the Committee were assured by the Department’s 
representatives that the remaining 2024-25 funds would be fully utilized by 31.03.2025,

strategic interventions to ensure efficient fund utilization in 2025-26. Proactive 
engagement with State Governments, NGOs, and implementing agencies is essential to 
streamline proposal submissions and disbursement process, particularly for skill training 
programs and capital expenditure. Furthermore, given the challenges in meeting fixed 
targets for schemes like SIPDA and DDRS, the Department should reassess target-
setting methodologies to ensure that they are realistic, flexible, and aligned with 
performance trends. The Committee recommend decisive action to improve fund 
utilization and program execution in the remaining year of the 2024-26 financial cycle, 
ensuring that allocated resources effectively advance the welfare of persons with 
disabilities and that the Department successfully meets its commitments under various 
schemes.

OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF 
THE GOVERNMENT ARE INTERIM IN NATURE 
 
(Recommendation Para No.8.3) 
 
The Committee emphasize the urgent need to expedite the establishment of the 
National University of Disability Studies and Rehabilitation Sciences in Kamrup, Assam, 
given the prolonged delays since its announcement in 2015-16. Recognizing the critical 
role of the university in advancing education, research, and rehabilitation for Persons 
with Disabilities, the Committee urge the Department to swiftly resolve land allocation 
issues, ensure timely compliance with the Department of Expenditure’s observations, 
and secure necessary approvals without further delay. The Committee recommend that 
a clear implementation roadmap with defined timelines be formulated to ensure the 
project progress efficiently, enabling the university to become operational at the 
earliest. 
    Reply of the Government  
The Department acknowledges the Committee’s concerns regarding the delays in 
establishing the National University of Disability Studies and Rehabilitation Sciences 
(UDSRS) in Kamrup, Assam. The Department has been actively pursuing the matter and 
has taken the following steps: 
a. Land Allocation: The initially identified land at Bondapara, Bekeli Mouza  under 
Boko Revenue Circle was found unsuitable as a significant portion fell within a 
reserve forest. Subsequently, in response to the Department’s request, the 
Government of Assam has identified and allocated 150 Bighas of Government 
Khas land in Village Deochar, Bangaon Mouza, Chaygaon Revenue Circle, 
Kamrup District. The Department has conveyed its acceptance and is awaiting 
the formal allotment letter. 

50 
 
b. Project Progress & Approvals: Given the change in the allocated site, the 
previously prepared Detailed Project Report (DPR) requires restructuring to align 
with the new location’s topographical and infrastructural requirements. The 
Department is initiating necessary revisions to the DPR, factoring in site-specific 
modifications and financial implications. Once the revised DPR is finalized, the 
proposal will be processed for further approvals. 
c. Implementation Roadmap: A departmental team has assessed the suitability of 
the allocated land, and necessary procedural formalities for land transfer are in 
progress. The Department remains committed to expediting the approval process 
and will ensure that all requisite clearances are obtained at the earliest to 
operationalize the University. 
  
With these measures, the Department is making concerted efforts to address the delays 
and remains committed to ensuring the establishment of UDSRS at the earliest.

CHAPTER-II 
 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No 1 Para 2.12) 
 
The Committee find that about 72.5 per cent of the Budgetary allocation of the 
Department of Social Justice & Empowerment is utilized on the Scholarships and other 
Educational Schemes of the Department. Keeping in view huge mandate of the 
Department to cater the needs of various marginalized sections including Scheduled 
Castes, Other Backward Classes, Denotified and Nomadic Tribes, Economically Weaker 
sections, Senior Citizens, Transgender, victims of substance abuse through various 
welfare schemes, the Committee urge that the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment should focus on other schemes also. For this purpose, if additional funds 
are required, they may seek more budgetary allocations. Further, the Committee find that 
there are frequent changes in the guidelines of various Schemes such as PM-AJAY, 
SHRESHTA, NAMASTE, PM-VISVAS etc. The Committee are of the view that the 
guidelines of any Scheme should be properly examined by seeking suggestions from all 
the stakeholders before they are finalized. In this regard, the Committee expect that the 
Department will find out the solution by taking into confidence the State Governments 
and also consider stepping up the budgetary allocation in future so that the Schemes 
other than educational schemes become meaningful for the targeted sections of the 
society. 
 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (D/o Social Justice & 
Empowerment) is mandated with the welfare, social justice, and empowerment of 
disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society. This includes Scheduled Castes, 
Other Backward Classes, Senior Citizens, Victims of Substance Abuse, Transgender 
Persons, etc. The department's goal is to integrate these groups into mainstream 
development and make them self-reliant. Accordingly, this department is running various 
schemes and fund allocation for all the schemes including scholarship schemes are 
made based on Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC)/ Standing Finance Committee 
(SFC) recommendations. Hence, in case of enhancement of fund for schemes, revision 
of EFC/SFC based on the need/demand and stakeholder consultations need to be done.  
  
It may be noted that NITI Aayog has issued Guidelines vide OM dated 25.01.2019 for 
earmarking of funds for Development Action Plan for SCs and STs (DAPSC & DAPST). 
As per the guidelines “As far as the nodal Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment 
(SJE) is concerned, the present level of earmarking of 72.5% of funds by the D/o SJE for 
SCs as recommended by the Task Force should continue”. 
 
Accordingly, in 2024–25, ₹10,309.0 Crore was allocated for the welfare of Scheduled 
Castes (SCs), accounting for 76.13% of the total budget allocation of the Department. 
Out of total budget allocated for SCs, ₹7420.65 crore was allocated for educational 
schemes for SCs. which is 71.98 percentage of SC welfare allocation. This leaves very 

8 
 
limited fiscal space for other welfare schemes. Similarly out of ₹2565.24 crore of budget 
allocated for Other Backward Classes (OBC), ₹2440.13 crore is allotted for education 
schemes for OBC, which is nearly 95 per cent of total OBC budget. Therefore, even if the 
overall budgetary allocations are increased, educational schemes are likely to continue 
receiving the largest share of funding. 
 
This being the final year of the 15th Finance Commission cycle, revising fund allocation 
at this stage may not be feasible. However, the revision process for the next cycle (2026–
27 onwards) is underway and will aim to address current needs, including additional fund 
demand. Inputs from stakeholders, including States/UTs and relevant Ministries, will be 
duly considered in the formulation of the EFC/SFC proposals.

Recommendation (Sl. No 3 Para 3.13) 
 
The Committee note that the Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ki Arthik Sahayata 
(VISVAS) Yojana for SC and OBCs was launched on a pilot basis in 2020-21 to support 
livelihood activities for marginalized SC and OBC with a 5 per cent interest subvention on 
income-generating loans upto ₹2 lakhs for individuals and ₹4 lakhs for Self-Help Groups 
(SHGs). However, the actual expenditure was 'nil' in 2022-23 and 2023-24 as the 
Scheme was not approved for 2022-23. Since the new guidelines for the Scheme were 
issued on 14.06.2024, the actual expenditure of ₹1.50 crore and ₹1.00 crore could only 
be made out of allocated funds of₹ 11.49 crore and ₹11.95 crore under the VISVAS 
Scheme for SCs and OBCs, respectively in 2024-25 (till February, 2025). The Committee 
are not able to comprehend the reasons due to which the Scheme could not take off till 
2024-25 and the Department took almost two years in finalizing the guidelines even after 
the third-party evaluation report was submitted in February, 2022. The Committee are of 
the opinion that any new Scheme should be launched after exhaustive consultations with 
all the State Governments, stakeholders, banks and other implementing agencies. The 
Committee desire that some mechanism should be evolved for the periodic review of 
Schemes so that the flaws are noticed and the requisite changes are made in the 
guidelines to plug the loopholes found during the implementation. The Committee would 
like to be informed of the instructions issued in this regard. 
 
 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
The VISVAS Scheme was initially approved for implementation in 2020–21 on a pilot 
basis, with further continuation subject to a third-party evaluation. The evaluation report 
was submitted in February 2022. Subsequently, a draft SFC note was uploaded by the 
Department on 12.12.2022 to seek comments from other Ministries/Departments, and an 
SFC meeting was scheduled on 23.12.2022. 
However, the Department of Expenditure (DoE), vide OM dated 23.12.2022, clarified that 
only in-principle approval had been granted for the pilot Scheme for 2020–21, and 
therefore, the scheme should not be treated as a continuing scheme under existing 
guidelines. Accordingly, a fresh Concept Note was submitted to DoE on 26.09.2023. In-
principle approval for implementation during 2024–25 and 2025–26 was granted by DoE 

11 
 
on 22.02.2024. The SFC meeting was convened on 09.04.2024, and the revised 
guidelines were issued on 14.06.2024, after the Model Code of Conduct concluded. 
The delay in relaunching the scheme was primarily due to procedural requirements and 
the need for fresh approvals. The initial evaluation conducted in 2021–22 formed the 
basis for the redesigned scheme launched in 2024–25. As the scheme is approved till 
2025–26, a fresh evaluation is currently underway to assess its outcomes and consider 
further improvements for its extension during the next cycle of Finance Commission. A 
budget provision of ₹23.44 crore was made under RE 2024–25, which has been fully 
utilized.  
Periodic review mechanisms, as suggested by the Committee, are being incorporated 
into the scheme framework to enable timely course correction and improved 
implementation. Additionally, the implementing corporations currently monitor day-to-day 
progress through regular meetings with their channelizing agencies. Review meeting in 
the department also takes place on regular basis with the implementing Corporations for 
monitoring progress of the Scheme. The Committee’s suggestion for institutionalizing 
such reviews will be factored into the design of subsequent extensions of the scheme.

 Online Registration & Submission: Fully digital process with user-friendly interface. 
 Real-Time Document Verification: Integrated APIs ensure authenticity and speed. 
 Enhanced Efficiency: Significant reduction in turnaround time (TAT) and improved 
transparency.
