Recommendation (Sl. No 8 Para 8.22) 
 
The Committee note that under SHRESHTA Scheme, the Residential Schools are 
selected from across the States/UTs on the recommendations of CBSE and State Boards 
to provide high quality residential education from class IX to XII to meritorious students 
form Scheduled Caste communities. The Committee find that 144 Private residential 
schools were selected to accommodate 3000 students on the basis of NTA examination 
during the year 2023-24 and 2024-25 under the scheme. The Committee note that an 
annual fee between ₹1,00,000 to ₹1,35,000 is granted to schools for each student taking 
admission in the Residential Schools. The Committee were informed that the students 
are getting admission in schools across the country as per their performance in NTA 
examination and preference made by the students. The Committee find that the students 
selected for admission are provided bridge course of 3 months to cover the study missed 
due to the time consumed in completion of the admission process. The Committee desire 
that the admission process should be completed in each school by the time academic 
session begins so that the students do not undergo any pressure due to delay in 
admission. The Committee feel that the fee fixed for each student is not sufficient to meet 
boarding, tuition fee expenses and other infrastructure required to provide ton class 
education to the students. Therefore, there is a need to have inbuilt mechanism for 
review and revision of the fee in order to maintain standards of top class education. The 
Committee during the study visit to one of the schools under SHRESHTA, while 
interacting with the students who are coming from other States, observed that it is difficult 
for a school student to cope up with different socio-cultural and linguistic environment. 
The Committee, therefore, desire that the Department may examine the entire process to 
explore the possibility that a student get admission in their domicile State. Hence, the 
Department should evolve a mechanism where a student is provided admission in a Top 
Class Residential Schools selected in their domicile State. In view of the foregoing, the 
Committee recommend that the Department would revise the Scheme at the earliest and 
apprise the Committee in this regard. 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
During the year 2021-22, the annual fee for class 9th & 10th was ₹75000/-per student and 
for class 11th &12th it was ₹1.25 Lakh per student. This was increased to 1.00 Lakh for 
class 9th,  1.10 Lakh for Class 10th, 1.25 Lakh for Class 11th, and 1.35 Lakh for class 12th 
during 2022-23. However, the need to revise these ceilings have been duly noted for 
incorporation in the scheme guidelines in the EFC for next Financial Commission Cycle 
starting from 2026-27. 
 
Further, it is mentioned here that the scheme is approved till 2025-26 and selection 
process of SC for Residential Education for the academic year 2025-26 has already 
started. Exam schedule has also been published on public domain. NTA has been 
requested to conduct the SHRESHTA (NETS) exam in December 2025 for the academic 
session 2026-27 so that admission process can be completed before the academic 

17 
 
session begins and students do not undergo any hardship due to delay in admission. 
Further, any change in the guidelines of this stage, will more delay the selection process.  
 
On analysis the data, it has been found that 70% students get admission in their domicile 
schools. However, to increase the number of students getting admission in domicile 
states, following procedure is being adopted. 
 
(i) Candidates will be required to select two states in which they are interested to take 
admission; in case a seat is allotted. 
(ii) During the choice filling process, only the schools located in the selected 
states will be displayed. Candidates will be allowed to submit choices only from this 
filtered list. 
(iii) After allotment of a seat in any round, the candidate must download the Seat 
Allotment Letter and report to the allotted school to complete the admission process.  
    
(iv) If a candidate fails to report to the allotted school after any round of seat allotment, 
he/she will not be considered in any subsequent round of counselling.

Recommendation (Sl. No 1 Para 2.11) 
 
The Committee find that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment spent 
6,410.09 crore and ₹7,830.26 crore on various Scholarships and other educational 
schemes in 2022- 23 and 2023-24 respectively. Similarly, in the year 2024-25, the 
Department has spent ₹3,403.51 crore on Educational Scholarship Schemes till 
February, 2025. The Committee appreciate the efforts of the Department in making 
education accessible to the deprived sections of the Society through various Schemes. 
The Committee believe that for the success of any educational scheme, other factors are 
also significant such as cost of education, availability of good Government 
Schools/Colleges and teaching staff for its effective implementation. The Committee are 
of the opinion that the annual scholarship granted to a student for pursuing education is 
not sufficient to meet the present-day expenditure required to get proper and quality 
education. The Committee would, therefore, like the Department of Social Justice & 
Empowerment to review the annual scholarship amount granted to each student pursuing 
various courses alongwith the Ministry of Education and other stakeholders to achieve 
the envisaged objectives of the various scholarship schemes of the Department. The 
Committee would like to recommend that the quantum of Scholarship granted to a 
student under each Scheme should be periodically reviewed to contain the inflation so 
that the Scheme is more fruitful. 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
The Department remains committed to ensuring equitable access to quality education for 
SC and OBC students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Concerns regarding the 
adequacy of annual fees and scholarship amounts under schemes such as SHRESHTA, 
SHREYAS (for SCs and OBCs), PM YASASVI, and the Post-Matric and Pre-Matric 
scholarships for SCs etc. have been duly acknowledged. As the current scheme 
guidelines are valid until FY 2025–26, and this being the final year of the 15th Finance 
Commission cycle, revising scholarship rates at this stage may not be feasible. However, 
the revision process for the next cycle (2026–27 to 2030-31) is underway and will aim to 
address current needs, including inflation adjustments. Inputs from stakeholders, 
including States/UTs and relevant Ministries, will be duly considered in the formulation of 
the revised guidelines. 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No 3 Para 3.14) 
 
The Committee find that ₹251 crore has been earmarked with the aim of benefitting 15 
lakh beneficiaries during 2024-25 and 2025-26 under the Scheme. The Committee also 
find from the figures given by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment that 
financial assistance of only ₹3.00 crore benefitting 47,809 OBC individuals and ₹4.452 
crore benefitting 44,006 SC individuals have been provided in 2024 25. The Committee 
find that even after the issuance of revised guidelines, the Scheme is not attracting 
targeted beneficiaries. The Committee believe that the target of 15 lakh beneficiary fixed 
for 2024-25 and 2025-26 is very difficult to be achieved. The Committee, therefore, 
desire that the reasons due to which Scheme is not picking up should be identified. The 
initiatives taken by the Department to promote the Scheme may yield desired results if 

19 
 
concerted efforts by the Department including NSFDC, NBCFDC, NSKFDC and Banks 
are made to make the Scheme successful. Since the Scheme is to be initially 
implemented in 2024-25 and 2025-26, the Committee are concerned about the tenure of 
the Scheme and desire that the Department should consider extending the tenure of the 
Scheme as the tenure of two years is too less for any Scheme to be successful. 
 
 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
The initial estimate of 15 lakh beneficiaries under the VISVAS Interest Subvention 
Scheme was based on a projected outlay of ₹251 crore, with on boarding scheduled 
across 2024–25 and 2025–26. 
In 2024-25, 7.96 lakh claims have already been received from BC, SC, and Safai 
Karamchari beneficiaries on the VISVAS portal, surpassing the annual target of 6.96 lakh 
beneficiaries. However, against a projected requirement of ₹97.5 crore in the Revised 
Estimates for 2024–25, only ₹23.44 crore was allocated, which was fully utilized. This 
funding shortfall has limited beneficiary coverage so far. During 2025-26, BE of ₹50.27 
crore has been allocated against the demand of ₹96.00crore. 
With the said allocation subvention benefit to 5.83 lakh beneficiaries will be provided 
during the two years duration of the scheme. 
While the scheme was initially approved for two years (2024–25 and 2025–26), it 
includes provision to meet committed liabilities until 2030. Given the evident demand, the 
uncovered but already on boarded beneficiaries will be progressively supported, 
especially as the scheme is likely to continue over the 16th Finance Commission period. 
To sustain momentum, continuous efforts are being made to raise awareness through 
channel partners. Standard IEC materials have been shared to support promotion and 
beneficiary outreach.

early finalization of the new Scheme with detailed guidelines for all the implementing 
agencies. The Committee may like to be apprised of the current status and the time by 
which the new Scheme is likely to be launched. 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
It is clarified that the Venture Capital Fund (VCF) Scheme is not being discontinued. 
Rather, it is being transitioned into a new and enhanced scheme with broader scope, 
improved coverage, and a more robust funding architecture. The existing VCF scheme 
will remain operational till 31.03.2025 and crucially, the investment period extends up to 
31.03.2029, by which time the fund is expected to be fully deployed. This ensures 
continuity of support to SC entrepreneurs while enabling a smooth shift to the upgraded 

20 
 
framework. The proposed scheme builds on the strengths of the existing VCF and 
incorporates critical feedback from stakeholder consultations and the findings of the IIPA 
evaluation study. 
 
A.  Incorporation of IIPA Evaluation Findings: 
 
The key concerns raised by IIPA—such as limited dissemination, inadequate grievance 
redressal, and challenges in loan support—have been carefully addressed in the revised 
Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC) proposal. The restructured scheme introduces 
several enhancements, including: 
 
 Promotion of Grassroots Entrepreneurship: With targeted outreach, 
awareness-building, and handholding support for first-generation SC entrepreneurs. 
 Strengthened Capacity Building and Mentorship: 
o Continued support through the “Aye Mentor” platform, offering structured 
digital mentorship. 
o Convergence with existing mentorship frameworks of DPIIT, such as the 
Mentorship, Advisory, MAARG, to expand access to sectoral experts, accelerators, and 
incubators. 
o A hybrid mentorship model, combining virtual and in-person guidance, 
especially in underserved geographies. 
 Accelerated and Transparent Funding Mechanism: Digital application and 
monitoring through the FINTECH portal, enabling faster turnaround and greater 
accountability. 
 Improved Grievance Redressal System: Integration of a time-bound, tech-
enabled redressal framework within the portal itself. 
These reforms complement systemic improvements already operational, such as 
digitized application processing, real-time verification, and the on-going on boarding of 
mentors and partners. 
 
B. Current Status of the Revised Proposal: 
 
The revised EFC memorandum for the new scheme has been formulated with a 
comprehensive, outcome-oriented design. It is currently under inter-ministerial 
consultation prior to submission to the Department of Expenditure. The proposed scheme 
is aligned with national priorities for inclusive development and is expected to drive 
scalable, SC-led entrepreneurship. 
The existing VCF fund remains operational up to 31.03.2025, with the investment period 
extending till 31.03.2029, ensuring continued financial support during the transition to the 
new scheme. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

21 
 
 
 
CHAPTER-IV 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No 5 Para 5.12) 
 
The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment is 
implementing Pradhan Mantri Dakshata Aur Kushalata Sampana Hitgrahi (PM-DAKSH) 
for SC, OBC and others since 2020-21. It is found that during the year 2022-23 and 
2023-24, the Department was able to spend ₹14.94 crore out of RE of ₹84.00 crore, 
₹58.34 crore out of RE of ₹140.00 crore respectively. Further, the Department has not 
been able to spend even a single rupee in 2024-25 till February, 2025 out of Revised 
Estimate of ₹80.00 crore as empanelment of Training Institutes was delayed. The 
Committee are concerned with the socio-economic development of SC, OBC and others, 
hence, believe that any slackness on behalf of the concerned authorities would defeat 
the purpose of the Scheme. The Committee are of the opinion that the Schemes 
instituted with the noble objectives cannot be left at the mercy of the concerned 
authorities, particularly when the Government of India is making all efforts for the socio- 
economic development of the targeted communities by allocating huge funds. The 
Committee would therefore, like to recommend that in future all necessary steps are 
taken to ensure that the empanelment of Training Institutes, etc. is not delayed and the 
necessary formalities are timely completed. The Committee would like the Department to 
take necessary measures so that the targets fixed are achieved. The Committee would 
also like the Department to enhance the targets keeping into consideration the population 
of these categories i.e., SC, OBC and others so that the maximum people can take 
benefit of the Scheme. 
 
 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
PM-DAKSH Scheme is being implemented by three Corporations of DoSJE, i.e. 
NBCFDC, NSKFDC and NSFDC. The Corporations are entrusted with the responsibilities 
of examining the claims/bills of the Training Institutes (TIs) and making payment against 
them as per the provisions laid down in Scheme Guidelines, Work Order and directions of 
DoSJE from time to time. As per claims/ bills received from the TIs, the Corporations 
submit request to DoSJE for release of funds. Therefore, the funds released by DoSJE 
are subject to the request received from Corporations in this regard. Recently, DoSJE 
has received proposals for release of funds under PM-DAKSH Scheme for settling 
pending bills of TIs and payment of the stipends to the trainees for the year 2022-23 and 
2023-24. ₹37.5 Cr to NBCFDC, ₹36.32 Cr to NSFDC and ₹5.58 Cr to NSKFDC has been 
released by the Department in 2024-25. As per the recent information submitted by all 
three Corporations, a total of ₹62.74 Cr has been released by the Corporations for 
training conducted in 2023-24 out of 2024-25 Budget. Further, it is informed that this 
Department spent ₹58.34 Cr in 2023-24. 
 
 
 
 
 

22 
 
 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No 5 Para 5.13) 
 
The Committee have found that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has 
sent a proposal to Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship to merge the PM- 
DAKSH Scheme with the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) Scheme in 
order to improve efficiency and optimize public expenditure as the PM-DAKSH Scheme 
largely overlaps with the objectives and structure of PMKVY. The Committee urge that as 
the proposal has been sent recently, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
may ensure that the beneficiary targeted for 2025-26 are not affected. The Committee 
may like to be apprised of the status of the proposals received and also of the 
implementation of the Scheme in 2025-26. 
 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
  For the year 2024-25 onwards, a decision has been taken in this Department to 
merge PM-DAKSH Scheme with Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) 
Scheme of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). It was observed 
that all the job roles under which training is imparted under PM-DAKSH scheme are 
available on SIDH Portal and covered under PMKVY Scheme. Therefore, it was not 
considered logical to run same skilling programme under this Department. Further, the 
scheme was additionality to PMKVY Scheme under which SCs and OBCs are also 
trained under other schemes including PMKVY conducted by MSDE. As such the skilling 
of the target group would continue to be conducted for their upliftment under the skilling 
programmes of MSDE. 
 
As it has been decided to merge PM-DAKSH Scheme with PMKVY Scheme for 2024-25 
onwards, no proposals were sought by this Department for implementation of the 
Scheme for 2025-26. However, with regard to status of proposal sent by DoSJE to MSDE 
for merging PM-DAKSH Scheme with PMKVY Scheme, the proposal of merging the 
Scheme is under consideration in MSDE. 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No 6 Para 6.18) 
 
The Committee find that the proposals under Free Coaching for SCs and OBCs were 
delayed in 2024-25 due to late commencement of courses in the academic year 2023-24 
and some proposals are also expected to be received in the month of February/ March, 
2025. The Committee also note that the Department have revised the guidelines from the 
selection year 2023-24 to achieve the target. However, the Memorandum of 
Understanding required to be signed with Dr. Ambedkar Foundation by all the Central 
Universities to become part of the Scheme has been signed by 19 out of 55 Central 
Universities. The Committee would therefore like the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment to ensure that the MOUs is signed by the remaining Central Universities 
as early as possible so that the economically disadvantaged Scheduled Caste and other 
Backward Classes candidates are not deprived from availing benefits of the Scheme. 
The Committee also desire that the empaneled Central Universities may be persuaded to 
timely commence the classes without any further delay and take necessary measures to 
expeditiously release the funds to them.  

23 
 
 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
The direction of the Committee have been noted. Other Central Universities will also be 
requested to sign MoU for implementing the Scheme and empaneled Central Universities 
will be followed up to send proposals at the earliest. 
 
 
Recommendation (Sl. No 7 Para 7.24) 
 
The Committee note that the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment provides 
giving grant to State Governments and UT Administrations and the Institutions of repute 
to construct hostels for OBC Boys and Girls. The Committee find that out of 1095 hostels 
sanctioned by the Department, the construction of only 848 have completed and 247 are 
still incomplete due to Administrative hurdles, procurement and contracting issues, 
design and structural approvals, etc. The Committee desire that the 18 months period 
stipulated for constructions of a hostel should be strictly compiled by the respective 
Institutions, State Governments and UT Administration and any hindrance in the 
construction activity should be resolved within the least possible time so that the 
construction work do not exceed the prescribed time period. The Committee therefore, 
recommend that the Project Monitoring Units set up to monitor Projects may be directed 
to regularly monitor the construction work and take necessary steps to settle the issues 
hampering the construction work. 
 
Reply of Government: 
 
The Department has taken note of the recommendations of the Committee for 
compliance and is monitoring the project regularly.

A. TRIBAL RESEARCH INSTITUTES (TRIs) 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 3.14) 
 
5. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
 
“The Committee appreciate the initiative of Ministry of Tribal Affairs for 
establishing of ‘Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums’ as they acknowledge the 

2 
 
heroic and patriotic deeds of tribal idols who are otherwise often under-
represented in the mainstream history. The Committee note that the Ministry 
have so far supported 11 Tribal Freedom Fighters’ museums in 10 States to 
celebrate the lives and deeds of tribal heroes and inculcate a spirit of pride in the 
minds of tribal communities. However, the Committee note that out of 11 
sanctioned Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums by the Ministry, only 3, namely, 
‘Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Freedom Fighter Museum’ at Ranchi, 
Jharkhand, ‘Badal Bhoi State Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum, Chhindwara and 
‘Raja Shankar Shah and Kunwar Raghunath Shah Freedom Fighter Museum’, 
Jabalpur, have been inaugurated. The Committee would like to underline the 
slow progress in construction of remaining 8 museums, as they were sanctioned 
far back in 2017-18, 2018-19 and 2019-20, such as, Tribal Freedom Fighter 
Museums in Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Telengana, Gujarat and Mizoram 
which are yet to be completed. The Committee are also concerned for the Tribal 
Freedom Fighters’ Museums sanctioned for Kerala, Manipur and Goa in 2017-
2018, 2018-19 and 2020-21 respectively as they are still at DPR stage even after 
the lapse of several years. The Committee, therefore, recommend that the 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs may evolve a strategy for timely completion of these 
Museums. The Committee would like the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to ensure that 
the four Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums scheduled to be completed by 
November, 2025 and one by May, 2026, are completed by the stipulated date” 
 
 
6. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as 
under:- 
 “The projects for construction of Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums are 
sanctioned by Ministry of Tribal Affairs after the same is received from the 
State. The project is implemented by the State and could include state 
components beyond the Ministry. The identification of the land, floating of 
tender, selection of Project Management consultant and the implementation of 
civil and curation work are the responsibility of the State Govt. The Ministry 
releases the funds to the state taking into account the status on submission of 
utilization certificate and project Progress Report which is a continuous process. 
For early completion of TFFMs, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is taking various 
steps such as regular visits by nodal officers of the Ministry to the construction 
site of TFFMs to monitor/inspect the progress of construction work, holding of 
frequent review meetings/ Video Conferences at Secretary/Joint Secretary level 
with Tribal Welfare Department/Tribal Research institute(s) of State 
Government in which TFFM is under construction. Apart from this support is 
also sought from experts and institutions” 
 
7.  While appreciating the initiative of the Government to establish eleven  
‘Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums’ in 10 States to acknowledge the heroic and 
patriotic deeds of tribal idols, the Committee in their original Report had noted 
slow progress in construction of 8 museums as they were sanctioned far back in 
2017-18, 2018-19 and 2019-20 to the extent that 3 of the Museums were at DPR 

3 
 
stage. The Committee had, accordingly, recommended the Ministry to evolve a 
strategy for timely completion of these Museums and expected that the four 
Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums scheduled to be completed by November, 
2025 and one by May, 2026, are completed by the stipulated date. The Committee, 
are, however, not satisfied with the action taken reply as they expected that the 
Ministry would at least assure the Committee that they will ensure that the four 
Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums scheduled to be completed by November, 
2025 and one by May, 2026, would be completed as stipulated but the Committee 
do not find any such assurance from the Ministry. The Committee would, 
therefore, like to reiterate their earlier recommendation and desire that the 
Ministry should meet the targets and the timelines once fixed for establishing the 
Museums to avoid delay and cost escalation. The Committee would also like the 
Ministry to consider only those proposals where the State Governments are in a 
position to readily identify land, float tenders, select the Project Management 
Consultant etc. at the time of submission of proposal. In this regard, the Ministry 
may consider revising guidelines to fix the time limits for floating of tender, 
selection of Project Management consultant and the implementation of civil and 
curation work so that the State Governments are mandated to complete these 
formalities in the given timeframe.  The Committee would also like to be informed 
about the status of under-construction museums at Final Action Taken stage. 
 
B. EKLAVYA MODEL RESIDENTIAL SCHOOL (EMRS) 
 
    Recommendation (Para No.4.17) 
 
8. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
 
“The Committee note that 720 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have 
been sanctioned out of 728 targeted to be set up in the country to provide quality 
education to the tribal children from class VI to XII in their own environment in 
remote areas to enable them access to the best opportunities in education and to

allocation of ₹7,088.60 crore has been made for the year 2025-26 for EMRS 
Scheme which is 47 percent of the total budget of the Ministry. The Committee 
find that under the Scheme, out of budgetary allocation of ₹5,943.00 crore and 
₹6,399.00 crore in the years 2023-24 and 2024-25 ₹2,471.81 crore and 
₹4,748.92 crore (till 17.02.2025) were utilized respectively. The Ministry attributed 
the factors for low utilization of funds during the past two years to non-availability 

4 
 
of land for construction of schools, recruitment of staff, capacity building, digital 
learning facilities, etc. The Committee urge that concerted efforts are required to 
be made by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to overcome these hurdles so that the 
funds allocated for the Scheme are utilized fully and objective of the Scheme to 
provide quality education to Tribal students is achieved.” 
 
9.  The Ministry of Tribal Affairs, in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted as 
under:- 
 
 “During F.Y. 2023-24 and F.Y. 2024-25, 99.98 % of the revised budget allocation 
(Rs. 2471.81 Crore) for FY 2023-24 and 99.34% of the revised budget allocation

concerning construction, human resources, and students’ learning etc taken to 
ensure maximum utilization of funds are as under:

district collectors to address land and forest issues. 
2. Ongoing communication with state and district officials through letters to 
resolve land-related challenges. 
3. Active coordination with state governments on legal, ownership, and forest-
related matters; 67 land issues resolved in 2024–25. 
4. A detailed school-wise tracker was implemented for monitoring project 
completion. 
5. Administrative approvals and DPR processes streamlined, cutting approval 
time by half.

8. Land and construction issues discussed in Manthan Shivir 2024 and PM

“Taking the fact that out of 477 EMRS, 341 are functional in their own Buildings, 
the Committee desire that all the EMRS are made functional from their own

Ministry of Tribal Affairs OM No. F.No.16015/03/2025-PC {E file No. 29655} dated

Recommendation (Para No. 8.7) 
 
The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest 
Rights) Act, 2006 was enacted to recognize and vest the forest rights and occupation in 
forest land on forest dwelling schedules tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. The 
Committee find that out of the 51,03,764 claims filed by Tribals, 24,98,185 titles have 
been distributed by 31 January, 2025. The Committee also find from January, 2020 to 
February, 2025, out of total number of 629 grievances related to FRS received by the 
States/UTs, only 120 have been disposed off. The Committee strongly feel that there is 
an urgent need to set up an effective grievance redressal mechanism so that the claims 
filed by Tribals are settled within a time frame as State/UT Governments are taking time 
in resolving grievances filed by Tribals. The Committee also feel that vesting of habitual 
rights to PVTGs is also getting delayed as only three States/UT viz. Odisha, Madhya 
Pradesh and Chattisgarh have initiated the process till date. The Committee, therefore, 
recommend that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs are required to take suitable measures and 
direct all the State Governments/UT Administrations to vigorously implement the various 
provisions of the Act.  
Reply of the Government 
 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs, being the Nodal Ministry for administering the legislative 
matters of “Scheduled Tribes and Other Forest Dwellers Recognition of Forest Rights 
Act 2006” (in short FRA), has been issuing directions and guidelines from time to time 
on various aspects to ensure proper implementation of the Act. As per FRA and rules 
made thereunder respective State Governments/UT Administrations are responsible for 
implementation of various provisions of the Act and the Act is being implemented in 20 
States and 1 UT.    
As per the information received from States/UTs up to 31.03.2025, a total of 51,11,104 
claims (49,02,098 individual and 2,09,006 community) have been filed and 25,10,462 
titles (23,88,834 individual and 1,21,628 community) have been distributed to the extent 
of 2,32,66,968.21 acres (50,74,095.93 acres for individual and 1,81,92,872.28 acres for 
community) of forest land. A total of 43,72,409 (85.55%) claims have been disposed of 
under the FRA and A total of 18,61,947 claims (18,08,909 individual and 53,038 
community) have been rejected.  
The implementation of FRA is a State Subject and states have their mechanism.

Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) portal wherein a citizen can

Recommendation (Para No. 4.20) 
 
The Committee note that an expenditure of ₹1,09,000/- per student per annum was 
specified in the EMRS guidelines,2020. The Committee were informed that this amount 
was not sufficient since revision in dearness allowance, implementation of pay revision, 
revision in labour cost, inflation in food and other commodities have increased 
significantly and could not be met in the amount fixed in the guidelines. The Committee 
were informed that the amount has been revised by EFC to ₹ 1,47,062/- per student per 
annum w.e.f. 01.04.2025. The Committee are happy to find that EMRS were to be 
modeled on the basis of Navodaya Vidyalayas as per the approval of Cabinet. The 
Committee, however, note that the revision of recurring expenditure in NVS on mess, 
uniform and other direct expenditure on students is done from time to time and total 
average expenditure for a student in NVS is ₹1,56,000/- for 9 months of functioning of 
NVS. The Committee feel that since the modeling of EMRS is based on NVS, hence, 
the expenditure of EMRS should also be in comparison with the NVS. The Committee 
are also not convinced with the idea of including expenditure on salary head while 
calculating the expenditure per student per annum. They desire that the Ministry of 
Tribal Affairs should examine and calculate average expenditure for each student in 
EMRS by excluding salary head expenditure as the average recurring expenditure 
would be adversely affected as the salary expenditure would keep on increasing 
annually due to increase in dearness allowance and annual Increment. The Committee 
would like the Ministry to consider the above suggestions while calculating average 
expenditure for EMRS student and ensure that at least the average expenditure is not in 
any case less than provided under NVS.  
 
Reply of the Government 
 
The Ministry had provided a comprehensive comparison of recurring costs per student 
from 2018 to 2025 for NVS and EMRS, with a proposal for revision in the recurring cost 
per student of EMRS to Rs. 1,56,206/- in EFC 3.0 for F.Y. 2025-26, which was in line 
with the NVS recurring cost projected for the same reference period.  However, Ministry 
of Finance vide its OM dated 20.01.2025 in respect of EFC for EMRS 3.0, approved 
inflation adjustment in existing recurring cost of Rs. 1.09 lakh per student for balance 
EFC period i.e., for F.Y. 2024-25 to Rs. 1,40,059/- and, for F.Y. 2025-26 to Rs. 
1,47,062/- (Rs. 1,40,059/- + 5%). 
The suggestions in the Seventh Report of Standing Committee on Social Justice and 
Empowerment (2024-25), “idea of calculating average expenditure for each student in 
EMRS by excluding salary head expenditure” and, “ensuring that at least the average 
expenditure is not in any case less than provided under NVS” shall be duly incorporated 
while submitting fresh EFC proposal for continuation of the EMRS scheme beyond 
31st of March, 2026. "

Recommendation (Para No. 3.14) 
 
The Committee appreciate the initiative of Ministry of Tribal Affairs for establishing of 
‘Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums’ as they acknowledge the heroic and patriotic deeds 
of tribal idols who are otherwise often under-represented in the mainstream history. The 
Committee note that the Ministry have so far supported 11 Tribal Freedom Fighters’ 
museums in 10 States to celebrate the lives and deeds of tribal heroes and inculcate a 
spirit of pride in the minds of tribal communities. However, the Committee note that out 
of 11 sanctioned Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums by the Ministry, only 3, namely, 
‘Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Freedom Fighter Museum’ at Ranchi, Jharkhand, 
‘Badal Bhoi State Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum, Chhindwara and ‘Raja Shankar 
Shah and Kunwar Raghunath Shah Freedom Fighter Museum’, Jabalpur, have been 
inaugurated. The Committee would like to underline the slow progress in construction of 
remaining 8 museums, as they were sanctioned far back in 2017-18, 2018-19 and 
2019-20, such as, Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums in Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, 
Telengana, Gujarat and Mizoram which are yet to be completed. The Committee are 
also concerned for the Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums sanctioned for Kerala, 
Manipur and Goa in 2017-2018, 2018-19 and 2020-21 respectively as they are still at 
DPR stage even after the lapse of several years. The Committee, therefore, 
recommend that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs may evolve a strategy for timely 
completion of these Museums. The Committee would like the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to 
ensure that the four Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museums scheduled to be completed by 
November, 2025 and one by May, 2026, are completed by the stipulated date. 
 
 
Reply of the Government 
 
The projects for construction of Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums are sanctioned by 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs after the same is received from the State. The project is 
implemented by the State and could include state components beyond the Ministry. The 
identification of the land, floating of tender, selection of Project Management consultant 
and the implementation of civil and curation work are the responsibility of the State 
Govt. The Ministry releases the funds to the state taking into account the status on 
submission of utilization certificate and project Progress Report which is a continuous 
process. For early completion of TFFMs, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is taking various 
steps such as regular visits by nodal officers of the Ministry to the construction site of 
TFFMs to monitor/inspect the progress of construction work, holding of frequent review 
meetings/ Video Conferences at Secretary/Joint Secretary level with Tribal Welfare 
Department/Tribal Research institute(s) of State Government in which TFFM is under 
construction. Apart from this support is also sought from experts and institutions.

The Committee note that 720 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have been 
sanctioned out of 728 targeted to be set up in the country to provide quality education to 
the tribal children from class VI to XII in their own environment in remote areas to 
enable them access to the best opportunities in education and to bring them at par with 
the general population. The Committee also find that an allocation of ₹7,088.60 crore 
has been made for the year 2025-26 for EMRS Scheme which is 47 percent of the total 
budget of the Ministry. The Committee find that under the Scheme, out of budgetary 
allocation of ₹5,943.00 crore and ₹6,399.00 crore in the years 2023-24 and 2024-25 
₹2,471.81 crore and ₹4,748.92 crore (till 17.02.2025) were utilized respectively. The 
Ministry attributed the factors for low utilization of funds during the past two years to 
non-availability of land for construction of schools, recruitment of staff, capacity building, 
digital learning facilities, etc. The Committee urge that concerted efforts are required to 
be made by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to overcome these hurdles so that the funds 
allocated for the Scheme are utilized fully and objective of the Scheme to provide quality 
education to Tribal students is achieved.

Recommendation (Para No. 4.18) 
 
Taking the fact that out of 477 EMRS, 341 are functional in their own Buildings, the 
Committee desire that all the EMRS are made functional from their own buildings and 
not from rented or other Government buildings as these buildings may be lacking 
required infrastructure for a school. Since the Ministry have sufficient funds to set up 
their own infrastructure, the Committee also desire that a comprehensive action plan 
should be chalked out to make them functional from their own buildings and the 
construction work of each EMRS is completed in a stipulated period of 2-3 years. The 
Committee expect that the steps taken by the Ministry to make all Schools functional 
would yield the desired results only if the timelines are fixed to sort out the bottlenecks 
and their timelines are not compromised.  
 
Reply of the Government 
 
The Ministry takes note of the Committee's observation and agrees that setting clear 
timelines and ensuring their strict adherence is critical for making all schools functional. 
Efforts are underway to identify bottlenecks and implement time-bound action plans to 
address them effectively. However, it is pertinent to mention that many schools have 
been constructed and made functional in last one year and Ministry is committed to 
make all efforts to achieve target of making all approved schools functional. The 
achievements of EMRSs (From June 2024 to April 2025) in this regard is summarized 
as under:   
 Locations Approved -16 
 EMRSs have been made functional- 73 
 Construction Completed- 70

EMRSs are functional across the country.

Recommendation (Para No. 4.21) 
 
The Committee find that out of 728 approved EMRS, 288 schools are 
sanctioned/established under Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution at the cost 
of ₹5.00 crore each. The Committee may like to draw the attention of the Ministry of 
Tribal Affairs to their visit of an EMRS in Karnataka, perhaps established under old 
Scheme. The Committee found that the facilities such as food, mattress, utencils 

22 
 
including maintenance of the building were not up to the mark. The Committee find that 
many EMRS have been running without basic facilities and required infrastructure such 
as compound wall, labs, sports facility, additional classrooms, staff quarter, hostel 
blocks, furniture etc. To provide these facilities, a survey of such schools was done and 
211 EMRS were identified for upgradation out of which 167 EMRSs have been 
approved till date. The Committee feel that the EMRS set up under old scheme needs 
to be revamped in a stipulated time period and sufficient funds are sanctioned to them 
in tune with the funds being sanctioned for each new EMRS. Further, the day- to- day 
hindrances faced by Schools should be managed by the schools themselves and the 
management should be suitably decentralized so that day- to- day issues are not 
brought to them and NESTS is able to concentrate on the larger responsibilities.  
 
Reply of the Government 
 
The Ministry acknowledges the concerns of the Committee and concurs that EMRSs 
established under Article 275(1) require systematic revamping. In this regard, out of 211 
schools, proposals for the upgradation of 192 schools have been approved by NESTS. 
Additionally, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has sanctioned funds to the respective State 
Governments based on the proposals received to bridge infrastructure gaps, such as 
residential quarters, classrooms, and boys’ and girls’ hostels. 
A comprehensive assessment of these schools is currently underway to identify areas 
requiring further improvement. Necessary proposals will be taken to ensure that these 
institutions receive funding on par with newly established EMRSs and MoF will be 
approached. Further, in order to empower State Societies and Schools to take certain 
decisions independently, NESTS has been issuing various circulars and guidelines, 
such as streamlining fund release procedure, guidelines for admissions, vacations, 
engagement of outsourced guest staff etc. These guidelines/circulars are also uploaded 
on NESTS website for wider outreach.

BUDGETARY ALLOCATION AND EXPENDITURE 
Recommendation (Para No.2.6 and 3.10) 
5. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee note that the actual expenditure of the Ministry of Minority 
Affairs has gone down considerably during previous years. The Ministry could 
spend only ₹837.68 crore and ₹1,032.65 crore out of ₹2,612.66 (RE) crore 
and ₹2,608.93 (RE) crore during the year 2022-23 and 2023-24. The 
situation did not improve in 2024-25 as the Ministry were able to spend only 
₹919.10 crore out of budgetary allocation of ₹3,183.24 crore (BE) by 31 
December, 2024. The Committee have been apprised that the Ministry have 
not been able to spend the budgetary allocation as several Schemes such as 
Free Coaching and Allied Scheme, Nai Udaan, Scheme of Providing Education 
in Madrasas/ Minorities (SPEMM), etc, have been discontinued and PM-VIKAS 
Scheme launched in 2023-24 did not initiate. Further, the amount allocated 
during 2022-23 to 2024-25 under various Scholarship Schemes of the 
Ministry could not be spent because these Schemes are under consideration 
for approval since 2022-23 as they are being harmonised with the Schemes 
of other line Ministries, viz. Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and 
Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The Committee strongly believe that the Ministry of 
Minority Affairs are making all efforts to achieve the mission of the Ministry 
by streamlining and strengthening the prevailing System so that the 
deserving Minorities can avail the benefits of the Schemes and the funds are 
not misused. The Committee feel that the steps taken by the Ministry were 
necessary in order to harmonize the system with the welfare Schemes of 
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Tribal Affairs and 
hope that these steps will improve the implementation of the Schemes and 
enhance the socio-economic condition of six notified minority communities in 
the country. Since the Ministry of Minority Affairs are in process of 
streamlining/strengthening the prevailing System, the Committee expect that 
the necessary approvals will be obtained by the Ministry at the earliest so 
that the allocated Budget of ₹3,350.00 crore for 2025-26 is fruitfully utilised. 
The Committee, therefore, recommend the Ministry of Minority Affairs to 
vigorously pursue with the concerned Ministries/ Departments for the 
pending approvals and keep the administrative machinery of the Ministry 
ready for immediate implementation of the Schemes as soon as they are 
approved.” 


3 
 
6. The Ministry of Minority Affairs, in their Action Taken Reply, have submitted 
as under:- 
 “The Observations of Hon’ble Committee have been noted for compliance.  
Under the Nai Udaan scheme, financial support was provided to candidates 
who qualify in the preliminary examinations conducted by Union Public 
Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), State Public 
Service Commissions (SPSCs). No other Ministry / Department provide such 
support to their beneficiaries. Hence, in order to align with the practices and 
schemes followed by other Ministries and to attain uniformity, it had been 
decided to discontinue this scheme w.e.f. 2022-23. 
Under Free Coaching and Allied Schemes (Naya Savera), coaching were 
provided to students from minority community to empower and prepare 
them for competitive and entrance examinations. The New Education Policy 
2020 does not support coaching programs; thus, the Ministry decide to 
discontinue the scheme w.e.f. 2022-23. 
Scholarship: 
After taking cognizance of media reports in the year 2020 regarding 
siphoning of Scholarship fund, the matter was referred to the Central Bureau 
of Investigation. Also, States were shared suggestive measures to 
incorporate in implementation of Scholarship Schemes. 
In the year 2023, a third party evaluation study, conducted by this Ministry, 
highlighted some irregularities, wherein out of sampled 1,572 institutes, 830 
institutes were found to be either fake/ partially fake or non-operational. 
Observing the seriousness of the issue, Aadhaar based bio-metric 
authentication drive was conducted in which about 27 lakh students and 
verifying officials were to be verified. After the drive, about 18.87 lakh 
students were finally verified for the year 2022-23. Subsequently, in order to 
make the system more robust, Aadhaar Payment Bridge System has been 
introduced for disbursement of scholarships.  
In the year 2024-25, a special drive for verification was held in the North 
Eastern States wherein, fake beneficiaries and verifying authorities were 
recorded. These were for the academic year 2021-22 and 2022-23. This 
exhibited that due diligence was not done by the States in implementing the 
Scholarship Schemes of Minority Affairs in some institutes. States have filed 
FIRs in this regard. Besides, the States have been given additional list of 
suspicious institutes (based on red flags generated by National Informatics 
Centers- National Scholarship Portal) to get them verified/ inspected and 

4 
 
take punitive actions against fraudulent elements. However, reports from the 
states are still awaited.  
In order to prevent duplicity of benefits, MoMA has also asked all the States 
to integrate their State Scholarship Portals with the National Scholarship 
Portal so that de-duplication can be done and one-student one-benefit could 
be ensured. However, the efforts by the States are yet to take a logical 
shape. In such circumstances, approval of Schemes could not be accorded 
by the competent authority and thus, the Ministry could not spend allocated 
funds under the three Scholarship Schemes. This Ministry endeavors to 
implement these schemes at the earliest.” 
 
Recommendation (Para No.3.10) 
7. The Committee, in their original Report, had recommended as follows:- 
“The Committee find that the actual expenditure under various educational 
Schemes was very insignificant in comparison to the budgetary allocation as 
several Schemes such as Free Coaching and Allied Scheme, Nai Udaan, 
Scheme of Providing Education in Madrasas/Minorities (SPEMM), Maulana 
Azad National Fellowship, etc. have been discontinued and Pre-Matric and 
Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are pending for approval since 2022-23. 
The Committee feel that since the Schemes discontinued were in operation 
for several years, their sudden discontinuation would deprive the targeted 
beneficiaries from the benefits of these Schemes. The Committee have no 
doubt about the intention of the Ministry but strongly desire that the 
substitutes of these Schemes even if at all available elsewhere, the 
beneficiaries should be made aware of such Schemes by publicizing them. 
Further, the Ministry should take necessary measures for the Scholarship 
Schemes pending for approval as the financial aid provided under these 
Schemes is very important and any more delay will adversely affect the 
educational prospects of the students belonging to Minority Communities. 
The Committee may like to be apprised of the initiatives taken by the 
Ministry of Minority Affairs in getting the approvals of these Schemes.”

9. While examining the budgetary allocation, the Committee found 
that the Ministry of Minority Affairs was not able to spend the budgetary 
allocation made during 2022-23 to 2024-25 under various Scholarship 
Schemes as they were in the process of harmonization of the Schemes of 
the Ministry with the Schemes of other Ministries, viz. Ministry of Social 
Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Hence, the Ministry 
were recommended to vigorously pursue with the concerned Ministries/ 
Departments for the approvals pending for the early harmonization of 
Schemes so that the Budget of ₹3,350.00 crore allocated for 2025-26 is 
fruitfully utilized. The Committee, however, do not find any commitment 


6 
 
for the allocated Budget from the action taken reply of the Ministry. The 
Committee expected that the Ministry would take suitable action to stop 
the misuse of the Schemes by the State Governments, but the Committee 
find that problem still persists and the Ministry have not been able to 
establish the required mechanism in the States due to lack of cooperation 
from States. Reiterating their earlier recommendation the Committee 
desire that strong measures needs to be taken for the State cooperation 
to stop misuse of Schemes in their States and also take measures for 
harmonizing of the Schemes of the Ministry with other Ministries without 
any further delay. The Committee would like to be apprised of the 
outcome of the steps taken by them in this regard.

CHAPTER-II 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY 
THE GOVERNMENT 
Recommendation (Para No. 4.8) 
The Committee note that the Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing Pradhan 
Mantri Virasaat Ka Samvardhan since 2023-24 by converging five erstwhile 
Schemes namely Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and 
Nai Manzil. The Committee find that the Ministry spent ₹83.51 crore out of Revised 
Estimate of ₹169.00 crore in 2022-23. After the convergence of independent 
Schemes in PM-VIKAS, the Ministry could spend only 209.42 crore out of RE of 
₹325.86 crore during 2023-24 and ₹124.08 crore out of ₹230.00 crore upto 31 
December, 2024 during 2024-25 to meet the committed liability of 2023-24 and 
2024-25 relating to the erstwhile Schemes. The PM-VIKAS Scheme, however, could 
not be implemented during these years as the guidelines of the Schemes could not 
be approved. The Committee feel that the Ministry should have timely initiated the 
proposal for approval of guidelines to avoid the extraordinary delay. The Committee 
now expect that the guidelines have since been approved, the targeted 
beneficiaries will not have to wait anymore to avail the benefit of the Scheme. The 
Committee hope that the approval of the proposal to integrate the portal of the 
Ministry with National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) etc. will not be delayed 
and the tie up proposed under the Scheme with National Institute of Design (NID), 
National Institute of Fashion Technology and Expert Promotion Council for 
Handicrafts will be finalized and executed at the earliest. The Committee would like 
the Ministry to sanction the proposals received for approval without any delay and 
take necessary action to ensure that the proposals are approved in a time bound 
manner. The Committee may like to be intimated of the action taken in this regard.        
 
Reply of the Government 
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee has been noted for compliance. 
Since the approval of the PM VIKAS guidelines, the Ministry has signed 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with its knowledge partners including 
National Institute of Design (NID), National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), 
National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) and Export Promotion Council for 
Handicrafts (EPCH) under the scheme. 
The Ministry has held Screening and Empowered committee meetings with 
various stakeholders under the PM VIKAS scheme to deliberate and approve the 

8 
 
proposals received for implementation of the scheme by two (02) institutions 
namely Delhi Sikh Gurudwara Management Committee (DSGMC) and State Institute 
of Hotel Management (SIHM), Manipur for 31,600 and 7,950 beneficiaries 
respectively. 
The Ministry has also signed an MOU with DSGMC and allocated the project 
of 31,600 candidates under PM VIKAS Scheme. 
Ministry of Minority Affairs  OM No. G-20014/02/2025- Budget  Dated   
19.06.2025 
 
Recommendation (Para No. 5.10) 
The Committee note that the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) is being 
implemented since 2017-18 with an objective to develop community infrastructure 
and basic amenities in the identified areas for improving the quality of life of the 
people in the Minority Concentrated Areas. The Committee find that the areas 
covered under PMJVK were increased from 90 Districts to 308 Districts in 33 
States/UTs w.e.f. May, 2018. On the scrutiny of budgetary allocation, the 
Committee observed that an actual expenditure of ₹222.66 crore out of ₹500.00 
crore (RE) and ₹189.23 crore out of ₹550.00 crore (RE) could only be made due to 
the introduction of SNA during 2022-23 and 2023-24 respectively. The Committee 
are happy to find that the Ministry of Minority Affairs have successfully spent 
₹618.00 crore (till 31.12.2024) out of ₹908.90 crore (RE) allocated under the 
Scheme during 2024-25 since the problems faced due to the introduction of SNA 
system has now been resolved. The Committee hope that BE for 2025-26 has since 
been substantially increased to ₹1913.97 crore from ₹910.90 crore in 2024-25, the 
Ministry should make an action plan to utilize the allocated funds so that they may 
not be reduced at the RE stage. The Committee would like to recommend the 
Ministry to popularize the Scheme so that the proposals are received from 
concerned Organisations and State Governments and take necessary measures to 
approve the proposals received in a time bound manner. They would also like to 
suggest the Ministry to provide the technical and administrative support to the 
implementing Agencies so that they are able to send complete proposals and the 
unnecessary delay due to the receipt of incomplete proposals is avoided. 
 
Reply of the Government 
The observation of the Hon’ble Committee has been noted for compliance. 
It may be informed that the Ministry of Minority Affairs is putting all efforts 
to make the States/Union Territories compliant to the PFMS and SNA Guidelines, 
reduction in the unspent balances available in the States/UTs treasuries and the 

9 
 
completion of old approved projects. Regular Regional Review Meetings/ re-
conciliation are being done to pursue the States/UTs for speedy completion of the 
approved project units and to release the funds to compliant States/UTs.  
The BE for 2025-26 in respect of PMJVK Scheme has been increased from 
₹910.90 crore to ₹1913.97 crore in the financial year of 2024-25. As per the 
recommendations of the committee, the Ministry has already worked out and made 
an action plan to utilize the allocated funds for PMJVK Scheme timely.   Due to this 
an expenditure of ₹204.28 crore (upto 16.6.2025) has already been incurred under 
the scheme and released to the eligible States/UTs for implementation of projects 
approved under PMJVK. Further, many States/UTs are eligible for release of funds 
and it is expected that remaining ₹809 crore may be released to them during 2nd 
quarter. 
With a vision to usher the digitization of the scheme for effective monitoring 
and evaluation of works taken up at the grassroots level, the Ministry has also 
introduced new modules i.e. QPR reports, Drop module, UC module, big ticket 
projects module etc. in the PMJVK Portal. A two day’s National Workshop was also 
held on 07.05.2025 & 08.05.2025, in which States/UTs/CGOs were given hands-on 
training for effective utilization of these newly developed modules of PMJVK Portal. 
Further, a dedicated PMU team of PMJVK also deployed for regular monitoring 
and frequent communication with the respective Nodal Officers of the States/ UTs/ 
CGOs. These States/UTs/CGOs are also given technical & administrative support to 
ensure timely resolution of all their queries.

INTRODUCTION 
 
  I, the Chairperson, Standing Committee on Social Justice and 
Empowerment (2025-26) having been authorized by the Committee do 
present on their behalf this Seventeenth Report on 'Demands for Grants for 
the year 2026-27' pertaining to the Ministry of Social Justice and 
Empowerment (Department of Social Justice and Empowerment). 
2. The Committee considered the ‘Demands for Grants (2026-27)’ of the 
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment) which were laid on the Table of the House on 10 
February, 2026. After obtaining the Budget Documents, Explanatory Notes, 
etc., the Committee took evidence of the Ministry of Social Justice and 
Empowerment (Department of Social Justice and Empowerment) on 24 
February, 2026. The Committee considered and adopted the Report at the 
sitting held on 10.03.2026. 
3. The Committee wish to express their thanks to the Officers of the 
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment) for tendering oral evidence and placing before them the 
detailed written notes and post evidence information as desired by the 
Committee in connection with the examination of the ‘Demands for Grants 
(2026-27)’. 
4. For ease of reference observations/ recommendations/ comments of 
the Committee have been printed in bold in the body of the Report.

SHRI P.C MOHAN 
Chairperson

and Empowerment 
 

1  
REPORT 
CHAPTER - I  
 
INTRODUCTORY 
 
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment envisages to empower the 
socially, educationally and economically marginalized sections of the society including 
Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, De-notified and Nomadic Tribes (DNTs), 
Economically Weaker Sections, Senior Citizens, Persons engaged in act of begging, 
Transgenders, Victims of Alcoholism and Substance abuse. The vision of the Department 
is to build an inclusive society wherein members of the target groups can lead productive, 
safe and dignified lives with adequate support for their growth and development. 
1.2 The Programmes and Schemes of the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment are categorized into Central Sector Schemes and the Centrally Sponsored 
Schemes. The Central Sector and Centrally Sponsored Schemes are as follows:- 
CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES 
 
I.     SCHEDULED CASTES WELFARE SCHEMES 
1. Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS) for 
SCs. 
a. National Fellowship for SCs 
b. National Overseas Scholarship for SCs 
c. Top Class Education for SCs 
d. Free Coaching for SCs 
2. Scheme of Residential Education for Students in High School in Targeted Area 
(SRESHTA). 
3. National Action Plan for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) 
4. Venture Capital Funds (VCF) for SCs 
5. Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi Yojana for SCs (PM- 
DAKSH) 
 
 

2  
II.     SOCIAL DEFENCE SCHEMES 
1. Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood & Enterprise (SMILE). 
2. Comprehensive Rehabilitation of Persons Engaged in the Act of Begging. 
3. Comprehensive Rehabilitation for Welfare of Transgender Persons. 
III.    OTHER BACKWARD CLASSES WELFARE SCHEMES 
1. Venture Capital Fund (VCF) for Backward Classes 
2. PM DAKSH Yojana for OBCs 
3. Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS) for 
OBCs and EBCs 
3  (a) National Fellowship for OBCs 
3  (b) Interest Subsidy on Overseas Studies of OBCs 
4. Scheme for Economic Empowerment of DNT/NT/SNTs (SEED) 
5. PM-Young Achiever’s Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs & 
Others (PM-YASASVI). 
IV.    OTHERS 
Information, Monitoring, Evaluation and Social Audit 
 
CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEMES 
 
I. SCHEDULED CASTES WELFARE SCHEMES 
1. Post Matric Scholarship for SCs ** 
2. Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) * 
3. Strengthening of machinery for Enforcement of Protection of Civil Right Act 1955 
and Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989 ** 
4. Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others ** 
 
II.    SOCIAL DEFENCE SCHEMES 
1. Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY)** 
2. National Action Plan on Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) * 
 

3  
III.   OTHER BACKWARD CLASSES WELFARE SCHEMES 
1. PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India (PM 
YASASVI) for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs * 
2. Post-Matric Scholarship for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs 
3. Pre-Matric Scholarship for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs 
4. Boys and Girls Hostel for OBCs 
5. Top Class Schools 
6. Top Class Colleges 
* These schemes are 100% Supported by Central Government 
** These Schemes are funded on sharing basis with States and Union Territories. 
 
1.3 The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment also supports the following 
autonomous Corporations: - 
(i) National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC); 
(ii) National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC); 
and 
(iii) National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC) 
 
1.4 The Committee examines Demands for Grants of the Department of Social Justice & 
Empowerment every year. During the examination of Demands for Grants, the Committee 
examined the following Schemes of the Department of Social Justice & Empowerment: 
(i) Budgetary Allocation 
(ii) Vanchit Ikai Samooh Aur Vargon Ki Arthik Sahayata (VISVAS) Yojana For SCs 
And OBCs 
(iii) Venture Capital Fund for SCs And OBCs  
(iv) Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi (PM DAKSH) For SCs, 
OBCs and Others  
(v) Scholarships For Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHYREYAS) 
For SCs 
(vi) PM Young Achivers’ Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India For OBCs And 
Others (PM-YASAVI) 
(vii) Scheme Of Residential Education for Students in High School In Targeted Area 
(SRESHTA) for SCs 
 

4

2.8 In view of the surrender of funds during the Year 2024-25, the Committee asked, whether 
any assessment has been done with regard to the allocation of budget on each scheme. The 
Department submitted vide their written reply that the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment undertakes assessment and review of budgetary allocation under its schemes to 
ensure that implementation does not suffer for want of funds.  
 
(i) Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others and the Post Matric Scholarship 
Scheme for SC students, which are implemented through DBT mode, States/UTs submit realistic 
targets in their Annual Action Plans. These proposals are appraised every year by the Project 
Appraisal Committee (PAC) under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Department of Social Justice 
and Empowerment, generally in April/May. This appraisal process ensures that allocations are 
based on actual requirement and realistic beneficiary projections.  
(ii) Under SHREYAS-SCs, no separate assessment with regard to allocation of budget on 
each component has been undertaken; however, allocations are made keeping in view past 
expenditure trends and ongoing commitments to ensure smooth implementation during FY 
2025–26.  
 
(iii) Under PM-AJAY, the total outlay for the period 2021–22 to 2025–26 has been approved 
by the Expenditure Finance Committee. Allocation among components is governed by approved 
scheme guidelines and clearly defined criteria. As per the guidelines, up to 50% of the total 
allocation is earmarked for the Adarsh Gram component based on actual requirement, up to 5% 

14  
for administration, monitoring and evaluation, and up to 2% for construction of hostels in Central 
institutions, with the remaining funds allocated to States/UTs under the Grants-in-Aid component. 
Savings under any component are redistributed to other components or States/UTs against 
viable proposals, subject to scheme guidelines. These provisions ensure balanced and need-
based allocation so that the scheme does not suffer due to lack of funds. 
 
(iv) Under SRESHTA, no separate assessment exercise has been undertaken for allocation 
of budget; however, allocations are made in accordance with approved scheme guidelines and 
projected admissions to ensure continuity of support.  
 
(v) Under AVYAY, the Department regularly reviews scheme performance and coverage to 
ensure adequate budgetary provisioning. Over the last five years, the number of Senior Citizen 
Homes supported under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens has increased from 607 
to 705, reflecting enhanced coverage. Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, the number of assistive 
aids and devices has been expanded from 8 to 17, increasing beneficiary outreach. Periodic 
National Review Conferences with States/UTs and independent evaluation by NITI Aayog 
through the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO) also guide budget 
projections and strengthen implementation to prevent any shortfall in allocation; and 
 
(vi) Under NAMASTE, the budget is proposed based on yearly provisions approved under 
the SFC/EFC process, and regular reviews are conducted to monitor expenditure across 
components to ensure adequate provisioning. 
 
2.9 On being enquired with regard to the measures being taken to ensure that the funds 
allocated do not remain idle so that the targeted sections do not suffer due to procedural lapses 
at the level of States/UT Governments, the Committee were informed by the Department of 
Social Justice and Empowerment vide their written reply that has stated that: 
 
“Yes, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has evolved systems to 
ensure that funds allocated under its schemes do not remain idle and that the targeted 
sections do not suffer due to procedural lapses at the level of States/UT Governments. The 
mechanisms introduced in recent years have yielded positive results in improving 
transparency, accountability and timely utilisation of funds.” 
 
(i) Under the Pre-Matric Scholarship for SCs and Others and the Post Matric 
Scholarship for SC students, the schemes are open-ended and demand-
driven for all eligible students of recognised institutions across India. 
Applications are invited through a designated online portal and the Central 
share is released through DBT directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank 
accounts of beneficiaries. States/UTs are responsible for inviting 
applications and verification through their established mechanisms. The 
DBT framework and portal-based processing minimise the possibility of 
funds remaining idle and ensure that eligible students receive scholarships 
directly.  

15  
 
(ii) Under SHREYAS-SCs, being a Central Sector Scheme, there is no 
State/UT-wise allocation of funds. Funds are released centrally based on 
approved proposals and ongoing commitments, thereby reducing the risk 
of idle balances at the State level and ensuring timely support to 
beneficiaries.  
 
(iii) Under PM-AJAY, since FY 2021–22, ₹ 1712.56 crore has been released 
under the Adarsh Gram component and 13,947 villages have been 
declared as Adarsh Gram. Under the Grant-in-Aid component, ₹1527.43 
crore has been provided to 2,48,570 beneficiaries, and ₹ 177.63 crore has 
been sanctioned for 90 hostels covering 10,649 beneficiaries. The 
introduction of the SNA SPARSH system, PFMS-based monitoring and 
regular review meetings has helped reduce idle funds and improve 
transparency. The scheme has been onboarded on SNA-SPARSH with 
effect from 01 July 2025, enabling just-in-time releases and preventing 
accumulation of unspent balances. Releases are linked to utilisation and 
compliance, thereby safeguarding beneficiary interests.  
 
(iv) Under SRESHTA, funds are released directly to selected schools/NGOs 
under the Central Sector framework. Releases are linked to compliance 
with scheme guidelines, inspections and submission of Utilization 
Certificates, which minimises the risk of funds remaining idle and ensures 
that students continue to receive support without disruption.  
 
 
(v) Under AVYAY, the introduction of the SNA-SPARSH fund flow system, 
mandatory submission of Utilization Certificates, inspection-based 
releases and periodic review meetings with States/UTs have significantly 
improved fund utilisation. Releases to States/UTs and NGOs are linked to 
implementation progress, compliance verification and physical 
inspections. In cases of delay at the State/UT level, the Department 
undertakes continuous follow-up and provides handholding support so that 
benefits to senior citizens are not adversely affected.  
 
(vi) Under NAMASTE, centralised procurement of PPE kits for sanitation 
workers and safety devices for Emergency Response Sanitation Units is 
undertaken and supplies are delivered to States/UTs for onward 
distribution. This centralised model reduces delays and ensures that 
beneficiaries receive equipment in a timely manner. The mechanisms 
introduced in recent years have yielded positive results in improving 
transparency, accountability and timely utilisation of funds.  
 
 

16  
2.10 On being asked about the States/ UT that have expressed inability in complying to the 
prescribed procedure for allocation/ disbursement of funds to the beneficiaries, the Committee 
were inter-alia informed vide written reply that: 
 
“Release of Central share is contingent upon States/UTs sharing their paid data on the 
designated Scholarship Portal. No specific report has been received from States/UTs indicating 
inability to comply with the prescribed procedure, however, timely sharing of verified data 
remains essential for smooth release of funds. Under PM-AJAY, which is implemented through 
the SNA-SPARSH mechanism, States/UTs are required to create scheme-wise State Linked 
Schemes, designate a Single Nodal Agency, open drawing accounts in RBI, close earlier SNA 
accounts, map schemes correctly and raise bills accordingly. Under PM-AJAY some 
States/UTs have reported procedural constraints such as delays in on boarding under SNA-
SPARSH, returning balances to the Consolidated Fund of India and closure of earlier SNA 
accounts. These procedural issues have contributed to delays in fund utilisation during FY 
2025–26. The Department has been regularly conducting review meetings, providing 
handholding support and issuing necessary guidance to resolve these issues and ensure 
compliance.” 
 
 
2.11  In this context, the representative of the Department of Social Justice and 
Empowerment, further updated during deliberation that: 
 
“As of now, we have spent around ₹ 8,159 crore. The updated figure stands at ₹ 8,277 
crore, which is close to 70 per cent of the RE allocation. In comparison, by February, 2025 
last year, expenditure stood at ₹ 6,799 crore, which represented 65 per cent utilisation. 
Therefore, our performance this year is significantly better. We are confident not only of 
reaching the RE target but of surpassing it, as we have sought additional funds under one 
scheme and have a substantial number of proposals under various schemes currently 
under process. We are, therefore, confident of fully utilising the RE this year.” 
 
 
2.12 As regards to the measures taken for full utilization of funds allocated for 2026-27, the 
Committee were inter-alia informed that: 
 
“For 2026–27, the Department is committed to ensuring full utilisation of Budget 
Estimates and avoiding downward revision at the RE stage through revision of scheme 
guidelines, streamlined fund flow under SNA-SPARSH, strict monitoring of utilisation, time-
bound processing of proposals and regular review with States/UTs to ensure that the allocated 
funds are fully and effectively spent. For FY 2026–27, the Department will further strengthen 
monitoring of procedural compliance, streamline processes under DBT and SNA-SPARSH, 
conduct regular review meetings with States/UTs and provide continued technical and 
administrative support to ensure timely allocation and disbursement of funds to beneficiaries 
without procedural delays. For FY 2026–27, the Department will continue to strengthen 
appraisal mechanisms, rely on realistic demand projections, undertake periodic performance 

17  
reviews, incorporate findings of evaluations, and rationalise allocations based on actual 
utilisation trends. These measures will ensure that adequate budgetary provisions are made 
and that none of the schemes suffer due to insufficient allocation. For FY 2026–27, the 
Department will further strengthen monitoring through SNA-SPARSH and PFMS, ensure just-
in-time releases linked to utilisation, conduct regular review meetings and field inspections, and 
intensify follow-up with States/UTs wherever delays are noticed. These measures will ensure 
that allocated funds are promptly utilised and that the targeted sections of society do not suffer 
due to procedural or administrative lapses at any level.” 
 
 
2.13 The Committee appreciate that the BE has been continuously increased over the 
last few years. From ₹ 12847 cr in 2023-24 it has now been increased to ₹ 13687.59 cr for 
the year 2026-27.The Committee however are not pleased to note that the Department of 
Social Justice and Empowerment has not been able to spend the allocated amount over 
all  these years. Even in the year 2025-26, ₹7317.95 crore only has been spent out of the 
Revised Estimates of ₹11402.74 crore. The Department still has a balance of almost 30 
percent of the Revised Estimates, even though the financial year 2025–26 is about to end. 
The Committee are also concerned to note that the Budget Estimates is invariably reduced 
by almost 25 to 30 percent every year at the time of the revision of estimates. The 
Committee do not find this to be a good indicator with regard to the performance of the 
Department. The hurdles in implementing Schemes, due to which the estimates are to be 
revised downwards or the funds remain unspent, should not be a recurring feature. These 
issues need to be resolved within a specific time period. The Committee, therefore, expect 
that the factors such as onboarding of States/UTs on SNA-SPARSH, submission of 
Utilization Certificates, release of matching shares by the State Governments, etc., will be 
sorted out in this financial year so that there is no more hinderance in the implementation 
of the Schemes. The Committee are optimistic with regard to the changes proposed to 
Expenditure Finance Committee of the Ministry of Finance in the Schemes of the 
Department of Social justice and expect that once approved for next financial cycle of 
2026-27 to 2030-31 will not only benefit but also boost the morale of the deprived sections 
of society. 
2.14 The Committee find that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
surrendered ₹2345.1897 crore out of ₹10309.00 crore sanctioned for the Scheduled Caste 
Division in 2024-25. Similarly, the Department surrendered ₹540.3672 crore out of 
₹2064.41 crore sanctioned to the Backward Classes Division and ₹79.5324 crore out of 
₹412.4600 crore sanctioned for the Social Defence Division. The Committee are unable to 

18  
comprehend the reasons due to which large portion of the allocation had to be 
surrendered in respect of the Schemes meant for the poorest of the poor section of the 
Society i.e., SCs, OBCs, EBCs and DNTs. Further, nearly 20 to 25 percent of the budget 
allocated for Top Class Education for SCs and Top Class School and College schemes 
for OBCs, EBCs and DNTs was surrendered by the Department. The Committee cannot 
draw any other conclusion than that the surrender of funds can take place only when 
either there is no proper assessment or the Implementing agencies are not strictly 
implementing the Schemes. The justification provided that the Department was in receipt 
of fewer proposals, delays in submission of replies, inadequate number of eligible 
admissions is not convincing to the Committee. The Committee are of the firm opinion 
that in a country where a large proportion of the population is young and requires proper 
education and skill development, the funds allocated should not remain unutilized due to 
the petty hindrances which can be resolved with little efforts. The Committee expect that 
the Department will take due care to ensure that educational schemes do not suffer and 
that problems arising in implementation are resolved immediately without any loss of 
time. 
2.15 The Committee are happy to note that the Budget Estimates have been 
successively increasing every year from ₹12847.02 crore in 2023–24 to ₹13687.59 crore 
for the year 2026–27. The Committee are however not happy to note that, the percentage 
allocation for the department of the total budget of Central Government has declined from 
0.29% in 2023– 24 to 0.26% in 2026–27. In the current scenario, when the Government of 
India is working towards the welfare of SCs, OBCs, EBCs, DNTs, etc., the Committee feel 
that the annual share of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment should 
increase rather than decrease. Though the decline seems to be marginal. The Committee 
feel it is a matter of grave concern and the Department should take it up with the Ministry 
of Finance. 
   Also, the Committee have no doubt on the sincerity of the Government but strongly feel 
that there is a lack of coherence between the Central and State Governments due to which 
there is under-utilization of Budgetary Estimates, resulting into surrender of funds. The 
Committee note that right steps are being taken by the Government for the welfare of the 
deprived sections of society but the hurdles in implementing is perhaps due to 
deficiencies in the mechanisms developed for smooth implementation. The Committee 
are, therefore, not happy to note that the same problems continue to recur and the 

19  
budgetary allocations continues to remain underutilized year after year even though the 
Department of Social Justice and Empowerment promises the Committee every year that 
it will fully utilise the funds allocated in the next financial year. The Committee’s main 
concern is that the citizens eligible for the benefits of the Scheme meant to improve their 
life are not deprived for the inefficiencies of others. The Committee hope that the 
Budgetary Allocation for 2026–27 will be fully utilized with minimal revisions and that the 
Department will take sufficient measures to break this vicious cycle. The Committee 
would like to be informed in this regard.

The Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Caste (SC) students is a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme, implemented by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment 
(DoSJE) through State Governments/Union Territory Administrations. This Scheme is currently 
in the final year of the existing Finance Commission cycle (2020-21 to 2025-26) till 2025-26. In
