REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
6. Noted. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
7. The Committee hopes that the spending pattern of  the Ministry and the 
organizations under its control will see an improve ment during the current fiscal.  The 
Committee desires to know the steps taken by the Mi nistry to ensure that the allocated 
funds are utilized optimally. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
8. The Committee would like to know the reasons for  not providing the grants-in-aid to 
IGRUA for 2015-16 and how the Institute would manage its expenses henceforth.  
     (Para No. 12 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
9. Regarding provisioning of grants-in-aid to IGRUA  it is to state that the management 
contract of IGRUA was awarded in the year 2008 with  the approval of the Cabinet. As per the 
terms of the management contract, Government will c ontinue to provide grants for the first 
three years from the date of contract and after tha t the IGRUA would be self-sufficient and no 
further grants is required to be paid by the Government.  Accordingly, grants were provided to 
IGRUA up to the 2010-11. However, as IGRUA could no t become self-sufficient after the 
year 2010-11 and Ministry of Civil Aviation took an  initiative to provide grants for next two 
years i.e. 2011-12 and 2012-13. In this connection the approval of the Cabinet for providing 
grants for the year 2011-12 and 2012-13 was obtaine d vide Cabinet note dated 7 
th  March, 
2014. 
10. Since the approval of the Cabinet for providing  grants-in-aid to IGRUA was up to the 
year 2012-13, no provision was made for the year 20 15-16. Regarding the management of 
expenses of IGRUA for the year 2015-16, it is to st ate that no decision has been taken in the 
Ministry as yet. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
11. The Committee is not satisfied with the reply o f the Ministry.  It is not clear from 
the reply whether the IGRUA is able to generate suf ficient funds to manage its 
functioning.  If not there is no ground for stoppag e of grants, the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation should take initiative to provide further grants till it becomes self-sufficient and 
no further grants is required by the IGRUA.  The Co mmittee urges the Ministry to 
expedite the decision on providing grants-in-aid to IGRUA. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
12. The Committee also notes that Rs.3 lakh was uti lized for Innovations in Governance 
during the year 2014-15. The Committee may be appra ised on the achievements made under 
this programme.  
   (Para No. 13 of ibid )  

 
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
13. Regarding the programme innovations in Governan ce under the Ministry of Civil 
Aviation, it is to state that this programme has no t been initiated as yet and no expenditure 
was done under this programme.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
14. The Committee notes the reply and feels that al location of funds for programmes 
which have not been initiated may be avoided so tha t these funds are allocated to the 
needy sectors.  The Committee may be intimated abou t the reasons for not initiating the 
programme - Innovations in Governance.   
Annual Plan 2015-16 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
15. The Committee notes that Rs.3341.50 crores has been allocated for the Ministry of 
Civil Aviation during the current fiscal against th e allocation of Rs.6711.74 crores at R.E. 
stage in 2014-15. There, the Ministry was able to g et only 49% of the previous year’s 
allocation, which is too meager to undertake develo pment of airport infrastructure and other 
related projects. The Committee feels that the Mini stry should pursue for restoration of 
budgetary support for its major organizations and i mportant activities, on- going or new, at 
RE stage vigorously. The Committee hopes that the Ministry would be in a position to expend 
the allocation under various heads judiciously and optimally during 2015- 16.  
   (Para No. 23 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
16.  Regarding reduction in budgetary allocation fr om Rs. 6717.80 Crore at RE Stage 
2014-15 to Rs. 3341.50 Crore for the FY 2015-16, it is to state that the major cut was imposed 
by Ministry of Finance for the plan budget of the Ministry from Rs. 6000.00 Crore at RE stage 
of 2014-15 to Rs. 2720.00 Crore at BE 2015-16. The cut under plan budget has severely 
affected the Equity Infusion of Air India under TAP /FRP. The Ministry has noted the 
recommendations of the Committee to pursue with Min istry of Finance for restoration of 
budgetary support at RE Stage.  
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
17. The Committee may be apprised of the further de velopment with regard to 
allocation of additional funds at RE stage.   
Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE 
18. The Committee finds that DGCA was able to get o nly Rs.50 crore out of the projected 
allocation of Rs.117 crore under Plan. The Committe e feels that this substantial reduction in 
allocation will hamper the efforts being made to up grade their facilities and activities. The 
Committee hopes that the DGCA will also improve its  performance in utilization of funds. 
The DGCA was able to utilize Rs.32.24 crore out of Rs.44 crore allocated at RE stage and the 
reason attributed for this is the delay in construc tion of new building for DGCA. The 
Committee is surprised to note that the proposed ne w building for DGCA has been stuck for 

several years. The Committee hopes that the land re lated issues are settled with the concerned 
Ministry at the earliest and the project is completed without further delay. 
   (Para No. 33 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
19. Ministry of Civil Aviation has allotted Rs. 50 crore under Plan Budget 2015-16 against 
the projection made by DGCA of Rs. 117.00 crore.  D uring 2014-15, DGCA has utilized Rs. 
37.14 crore out of Rs. 44 crore allotted under RE a nd made its best efforts to utilize the 
maximum funds upto RE level which is 84.40% of Revi sed Estimates during the Financial 
Year 2014-15.  
• It was initially decided to construct the new DGCA Bhawan at the existing site 
through CPWD. Since CPWD could not succeed in getti ng clearances necessary for 
constructing the building in Lutyen's zone, an alternate site for the same was explored.  
• For constructing the DGCA Bhawan, Ministry of Urban  Development had been 
requested since March, 2013, to transfer the title and ownership of land, opposite 
Safdarjung Airport where DGCA Office is currently l ocated since pre-independence 
days, alongwith A-2, Karbala Lane, in favour of DGCA.  
• The Land issues between MoCA and MoUD were placed b efore COS. COS in its 
meeting held on 23-08-2013, vide point 8.2 recommen ded that "MoUD would take 
decision regarding other unresolved land related is sues in accordance with the rules 
and communicate the same to MOCA. If required the a dvice of Ministry of Law may 
be obtained". The committee also felt that the Land  issues have to be resolved based 
on the facts of ownership based on land records, al lotment/ transfer of land etc in 
respect of individual cases. MoUD was to decide on the issue based on the facts of the 
individual case in accordance with the legal positi on. It did not deliberate on it further 
to give any decision indicating therein that the ne cessary details are not available 
before the COS. DGCA has followed up the matter rep eatedly with Ministry of Urban 
Development. A meeting was held on 14th May, 2015, under the Chairmanship of 
Secretary (Civil Aviation) to address the issues pe rtaining to construction of DGCA 
Bhawan. 
• In compliance to the deliberations of the meeting, a letter from DGCA has been issued 
to Ministry of Urban Development on 5th June, 2015,  requesting them to either 
declare Airports Authority of India as Civil Wing o f Ministry of Civil Aviation or 
agree to the request of a dedicated CPWD Wing under  administrative control of 
DGCA, transfer the title and ownership of plot of l and where the present DGCA 
building is located, to DGCA at the earliest. Respo nse of Ministry of Urban 
Development is awaited.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
20. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that is sues related to allocation of land

 97. Since, C of A, C of R, Aeromobile Licence were  expiring on 13.02.2015 due to expiry

106. The Committee notes there is lack of planning is returning the leased aircrafts.  
This shows inefficiency on the part of the manageme nt.  The Committee notes the reply 
and desires that the issues involved in returning t he leased aircrafts lying abroad are 
settled at the earliest.  The Committee may also be informed on the status of recruitment

RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
107. The Committee feels that adequate seats should  be reserved for last minute booking 
with affordable fares, for persons travelling in me dical emergency and persons accompanying 
a corpse or for the next of kin in case of bereavem ent in a family. The Committee also feels 
that large number of students from not so well to-d o background is going for higher studies to 
far off areas of the country and when they have to visit to their family, they lose at least 3-4 
days in travel to and fro; they cannot afford the air travel. The Committee is of the view that in 
such cases, some kind of concessional fare may be d evised (appropriately may be) under 
social obligation of the airlines. 
   (Para No. 102 of ibid )  

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
108. Air India always remains committed to assist c ustomers in times of need.   Air India 
offers fares that are competitive and market driven .  Offering specific fares, as suggested, 
entails reserving of seats to the last minute.  As seats are highly perishable commodity and 
once aircraft has departed, cannot be inventoried f or future sale by blocking of seats which 
may lead to loss of revenue and spoilage of seats. 
109. Air India offers 50% discount on the normal Ec onomy class fare on domestic sectors 
to Students studying in India for travelling betwee n Home Town and Place of Study and vice 
versa.  The concessional fare is 50% of Basic fare of normal economy class (Y RBD) fare and 
booking class is RBD ‘V’.  Tickets can be issued by  Air India offices, approved Travel 
Agents and through Air India website on 
www.airindia.in . 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
110. The Committee notes the reply.  The committee recommends that the facility of 
50% concession on basic fare may be extended to tho se persons travelling in medical 
emergency and persons accompanying a corpse or for next of kin case of bereavement in 
a family.  
Hotel Corporation of India 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE   
111. The Committee would like to be informed about the logic behind non-allocation of 
funds for HCIL during the current fiscal. The Commi ttee feels that the Government needs to 
revisit the necessity of the HCIL. The Committee ho pes that allocation of funds to Centaur 
Hotel Delhi, Centaur Hotel Srinagar and Chefair Fli ght Catering Delhi will be made 
accordingly. The Committee expects that the ongoing  renovation works in all the units of 
HCIL are completed on time.  
   (Para No. 108 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
112. Regarding allocation for the financial year 20 15-16 for HCIL, it is to state that the 
Annual plan projection was made to Ministry of Fina nce, but they did not allocate any fund 
for HCIL at BE stage.  However, in view of the reco mmendations of the Committee the 
requirement of funds for HCIL has been taken up wit h the Ministry of Finance in the 1 st  batch 
of Supplementary which has not been accepted by the m. However the proposal will again be 
taken up at RE stage. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
113. The Committee feels that Hotel Corporation of India is in dire need of funds to 
renovate its properties in order to face the stiff competition in the hotel industry.  The 
Committee desires that the Ministry may pursue the demand for allocation of funds for 
Hotel Corporation of India vigorously with the Mini stry of Finance and the action taken 
in this regard may be intimated to the Committee accordingly.   
Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
114. The Committee notes that the BCAS was able to spend Rs.15.14 crore only out of 
Rs.32.00 crore allocated at RE stage under Plan Hea d during 2014-15. The Committee would 
like to know the reasons for under-utilization of funds under Plan Head. The Committee hopes 
that the funds allocated for current fiscal under v arious Heads are utilized by BCAS 

judiciously. The Committee feels that the construct ion of new building for BCAS should be 
expedited and the pending issues on the project may  be sorted out with the concerned 
agencies. The Committee desires that filling up of vacant posts at various levels in BCAS 
should get due consideration during the current fiscal also, to strengthen its security apparatus.  
   (Para No. 113 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
115. Rs 15.50 crores were earmarked for Biometric A ccess Control System for which 
tender process could not be finalized during the financial year 2014-15.  The location and land 
has not been finalized for Re-construction of new b uilding for BCAS HQ.  Filling up of 
vacant posts at various levels in BCAS is under consideration. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
116. The Committee hopes that the BCAS will be able  to spend the allocated funds 
fully during the current fiscal.  The Committee des ires that the pending issues with 
respect to the construction of new building for BCAS should be sorted out at the earliest.  
The Committee may be further informed on the steps taken to fill up the vacant posts in 
BCAS. 
 
Indira Gandhi Rashtriya Uran Akademi (IGRUA) 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
117. The Committee finds that IGRUA has not been al located any grant-in-aid for the 
current fiscal and Rs.13.60 crore allocated for 201 4-15 could not be utilized fully. The 
Committee would like to know the sources through wh ich IGRUA will mobilize its funds so 
that it can take up its pending projects, for development/expansion.  
   (Para No. 115 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
118. A grant of Rs. 13.6 Crore was released on 30th  March 2015. This was the subsidy 
(Revenue) approved for Financial Year 2010-11 and 2 012-13. As this is revenue grant it is 
utilized for meeting its operational expenses.   Fo r development, IGRUA has recently been 
granted Rs. 5.10 Crore in Plan funds to set up an A ME School. Fully funded National 
Aviation University is being built on IGRUA campus. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
119. The Committee notes the reply. 
Aero Club of India 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
120. The Committee finds that Rs. 10 lakhs was prov ided as Grants-in-aid to Aero Club of 
India for flying training and aero sports development during 2014- 15 but the Club was able to 
spend Rs.3 lakhs only out of the allocation without  any valid reason. The Committee also 
feels that the Aero Club of India which is also wor king with the Ministry of Sports and Youth 
Affairs and State Governments to give training to p eople with gliders and other equipment, 
may be provided with necessary budgetary allocation at RE stage.  
   (Para No. 118 of ibid )  

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
121. Regarding grants-in-aid to Aero Club of India for the financial year 2014-15 it is to 
state that the entire allocation of Rs. 10 Lakhs wa s released during the last financial year. 
Regarding allocation for the financial year 2015-16 for ACI, it is to state that the projection of 
Rs. 26.00 Crore was made to Ministry of Finance but  they did not allocate any fund for ACI. 
The Ministry has noted the recommendation of the Co mmittee to pursue with Ministry of 
Finance for necessary budgetary allocation at RE stage.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
122. The Committee desires that the allocation of f unds for ACI may be taken up with 
the Ministry of Finance on priority basis and that the Committee may be apprised of the 
response of the Ministry of Finance in this regard. 
Civil Aviation Policy  
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
123. The Committee has been consistently emphasizin g the need to have a civil aviation 
policy for such a growing sector for which India ha s humongous potential. Now, it is happy 
that the formulation of Civil Aviation Policy is already in advance stage. The Committee feels 
that the views, comments and suggestions given by t he stakeholders from the aviation 
industry be given due consideration in finalizing the National Civil Aviation Policy.  
   (Para No. 120 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
124. Hon'ble Minister for Civil Aviation has unveil ed a Draft Civil Aviation Policy on 10th 
November, 2014 to address various issues related to the sector. Main features of policy related 
to Development of airports, Rationalizing the cost of Aviation Turbine Fuel (AM), 
Development of the Cargo sector, Institutional refo rms, Enhancing Regional Connectivity, 
Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) facilities, Modernization of Air Navigation 
Services (ANS), Development of Helicopter Aviation,  DGCA and e-Governance. The 
Ministry invited comments/suggestions of the public /stakeholders /State Governments on the 
draft policy. Finalization of Civil Aviation Policy  is being undertaken taking into account 
various suggestions received on the draft policy. T he matter is under consideration of this 
Ministry. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
125. The Committee notes the reply and hopes that t he draft Civil Aviation Policy 
uploaded in the Ministry of Civil Aviation’s Portal  for comments will be finalized at the 
earliest, after giving due consideration to the sug gestions/comments received from 
various stakeholders. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
126. As regards creating international hubs, Kochi International Airport which is handling a 
large number of domestic and international passenge rs and has already become a hub for 
international operations especially to Gulf countri es, the Committee feels, may be included. 
This airport has substantial international traffic and has immense growth potential. 
   (Para No. 121 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
127. Noted. 

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
128. The Committee reiterates its recommendation an d  hopes that the inclusion of 
Kochi Airport as an international hub will be expedited at the earliest.   
Regulation of Airfares  
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
129. The Committee finds that currently there is no  transparent mechanism to regulate the 
air fare in the country. As a result, airlines are free to charge as much as they can and the 
travellers also are caught unawares about it. The C ommittee does not agree with the argument 
of the Ministry that some rules/regulations under the Aircraft Act, 1934 regulate air fare in the 
country.  
   (Para No. 122 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
130. Presently, air fares are not regulated by the Government as they are determined by the 
interplay of market forces. Airlines offer fares on  various levels which are driven by demand 
and market forces and as the demand goes up the seats on lower fare levels get filled. This is a 
global practice in the aviation industry. Pricing f orms the strategic framework, day-to-day 
tactical changes in pricing to respond to demand/su pply and market dynamics is through the 
Inventory Management process. Airlines are required  to establish reasonable tariff under the 
provision of Sub-rule (1) of Rule 135, Aircraft Rul es 1937 having regard to all relevant 
factors, including the cost of operation, character istics of service, reasonable profit and the 
generally prevailing tariff. Airlines remain compliant to the regulatory provisions of Sub-Rule 
2 of Rule 135 as long as the fare charged by them d oes not exceed the fare established and 
displayed on their website. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE   
131. The Committee in view of the hardship faced by  common travellers and the air travel 
becoming a necessity cannot agree with this lame ex cuse, which is purely technical. The said 
Act and the Rules framed is more than 80 years old and the civil aviation sector during this 
period has gone a sea change. The Committee, theref ore, strongly feels that this Act/Rule also 
needs to be overhauled now. Secondly, the idea of providing a competition between airlines in 
this sector has not worked. Therefore, we are facin g the problem of predatory airfare today. It 
may also be due to some kind of cartelization among st the airlines. Even the benefit of 
reduction in the price of ATF is also not passed on  to the passengers as reduced in air fares. 
Therefore, the Committee strongly feels that this i s high time now that the Ministry must step 
in by putting a regulatory mechanism in place to se e that airfares remain within a reasonable 
range. The existing system has not worked. 
   (Para No. 123 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
132. The facts regarding air fare is as follows:  
• The Rule 135, the Aircraft Rules 1937 was latest re vised on 16/04/2009. Though the 
Act & Rules indicate the year 1934 & 1937, the revi sion of the Act & Rules are 
continuous process and have been revised from time to time as deemed fit by the 
Government.  
• The domestic airline pricing runs in multiple level s (bucket or RBD) which is in line 
with the practice followed globally. The lower fare  in the fare bucket is available for 

advance booking much earlier. As time lapses and da te of journey approaches closer, 
the fare in higher side of fare bucket is made avai lable as per the respective airline 
policy. In order to identify the fare and condition s of travel on passenger tickets, 
airlines world over follow IATA Resolution 728 whic h contains information on 
various booking classes referred to as Reservation Booking Designator (RBD). The 
RBD is the code used in reservation transactions to identify the booking class. 
• While the Government no longer regulates the fares that are charged, it is ensured that 
considerable information is provided to the public in a transparent manner with respect 
to airline fares.  
• Air Transport Circular 05 of 2009 was issued for sc heduled domestic airlines to 
display the airfare as per the template given in th e circular, compliant to Rule 135. For 
both domestic and international markets, carriers m ust provide disclosure of the full 
price to be paid, including government taxes/fees c arrier charges, as well as fees 
payable to airport operators in their advertising, on their websites and on the 
passenger's e-ticket confirmation.  
• To ensure transparency and aid the travelers make a n informed choice, DGCA vide 
Air Transport circular 02 of 2010 has directed the airlines to upload fare sheet 
displaying fare offered across their network. The f are sheet contains information on 
various levels of fares starting from the lowest (discounted fares) to full fare offered on 
all sectors. This is done on a monthly basis and updated whenever there is any revision 
of fares. DGCA also ensures the fare sheet is updat ed and tracks any deviation 
between fares offered and uploaded on the website on a regular basis. 
Air Transport Circular 01 of 2015 requires carriers to disclose all fees for optional services 
on 'opt-in' basis through a prominent link on their homepage. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
133. The Committee notes the reply.  However, it is  of the considered view that some 
mechanism to cap the maximum fares on every sector is needed. 
GENERAL OBSERVATION/RECOMMENDATION 
134. The Committee, on scrutinizing of budget paper s of Ministry of Civil Aviation finds 
that the overall performance of the Ministry during  the last year has been satisfactory, but 
utilization of funds needs further improvement. The  Committee also finds that the Union 
Budget 2015-16 shows a huge gap between projected d emand and actual allocation. For 
example, civil aviation sector was able to get mere ly 71% of the projected annual plan and 
49% of the previous year’s allocation at RE stage. The Committee hopes that allocation of 
additional funds for Directorate General of Civil A viation (DGCA), Bureau of Civil Aviation 
Security (BCAS), Air India and Airports Authority o f India will help these Organizations to 
complete various ongoing aviation projects under th eir jurisdiction. The Committee 
recommends the Ministry of Civil Aviation may take-up the requirement of budgetary support 
with the Ministry of Finance at RE stage vigorously. 
   (Para No. 124 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
135. The Ministry has noted the recommendation of t he Committee to take up the 
requirement of budgetary support with Ministry of Finance at RE stage. 

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
136. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and hopes that additional 
budgetary support for various projects are received  at RE stage so that these projects 
are not stalled/delayed for want of funds. 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
137. The Committee desires the creation of Civil Av iation Authority, absence of such an 
agency in India was pointed out by the Federal Avia tion Agency during its last audit. The 
Committee also had recommended about this. Subseque ntly, a Bill was brought before 
Parliament which was examined and reported by the C ommittee. The Committee hopes that 
the Bill including the recommendations of this Comm ittee in its 203rd Report (on the Civil 
Aviation Authority of India Bill, 2013) presented t o the Parliament in February, 2014 will be 
introduced in the Parliament at the earliest. 
   (Para No. 125 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
138. Cabinet Secretariat vide OM dt 20.05.2014 advi sed that the Bills, that has been cleared 
by the Cabinet in the recent past and are yet to be  enacted as laws, will need to be placed 
before the Cabinet for a decision as to whether the se Bills are to be pursued in their present 
form or any changes are required to be carried out therein. Accordingly, a revised Civil 
Aviation Authority of India Bill, 2014 incorporatin g some changes in the Civil Aviation 
Authority Bill, 2014 was circulated for inter-Ministerial consultation. 
139. During the course of inter-Ministerial consult ations, Department of Expenditure, 
Ministry of Finance has proposed that the matter ma y be first got appraised at the EFC/CNE 
prior to placing it before the Cabinet for its cons ideration. As per the advice of Department of 
Expenditure, an EFC Memo is being prepared, besides the CAA Bill is also being reviewed in 
view of comments received from other Ministries/Departments. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
140. The Committee notes that the Govt. is taking t oo much time to finalize Civil 
Aviation Authority which is unwarranted.  The Commi ttee hopes that the Civil Aviation 
Authority of India Bill will be placed before the P arliament at the earliest so that the 
proposed Authority can address all the grey areas in the aviation sector.   
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE   
141. The Committee also hopes that the Government w ill finalize the Civil Aviation Policy 
on priority so that all the issues concerning aviat ion sector in the country are duly addressed 
and the ever growing aviation sector gets much needed impetus from the Government. 
   (Para No. 126 of ibid )  
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT   
142. Noted. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
143. The Committee hopes that with the timely imple mentation of Civil Aviation 
Policy, the aviation sector will be able to overcom e the hurdles it is presently facing.   
The Committee also desires that Kochi may be made a s an international hub while 
formulating the Civil Aviation Policy.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
5.     The Committee notes that the present Budget Estima tes shows an increase of just 
Rs.10 crores in comparison to the Revised Estimate last year i.e.,  (2014-15). The Committee 
is also surprised to note that the Ministry had to face a sharp budgetary cut at RE stage in the 
last financial year. The Committee failed to get a convincing reason for this cut. Given the 
importance of the mandate of this Ministry i.e,  to preserve, protect and promote our vast 
cultural heritage, both tangible and intangible, sp read across the length and breadth of the 
country, the Committee is at a loss to see that Pla n allocation to this Ministry has come down 
from Rs.1835 crore in BE 2014-15 to Rs.1500 crore i n RE 2014-15 and to Rs.1455 crore in 
BE of 2015-16. Such allocation are highly insuffici ent and the Committee recommends that 
Plan allocation for the Department be increased adequately at RE stage.       
          (Recommendation at Para No.13 of the 219 
th  Report)

appropriate action in consultation with State Gover nments, to avoid delays in finalization of 
proposals. 
 FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
150.  The Committee notes the reply. 
Development of Jallianwala Bagh Memorial 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
151. The Ministry has stated in its Outcome Budget that though an outlay of Rs. 
1,00,000/-  was made in order to take up a comprehe nsive development of the Jallianwala 
Bagh Memorial, befitting its status and importance of the Indian freedom struggle, no grants 
was released during 2014-15. 
                                   (Para No. 117 of ibid 
)                                                      
152. The Committee notes the reply and desires to k now the reasons for the same.          
                                        (Para No. 1 18 of ibid )                                         
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
153. A project for Development and revitalization o f Jallianwala Bagh National 
Memorial was approved in 2007 and an amount of Rs. 751 lakhs was released by the Ministry 
of Culture to the Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial Trust during the period from 2008-2010 
in four installments. 

Out of this amount, the Trust released an amount of Rs.5.36 crore to Indian Tourism 
Development Corporation (ITDC), New Delhi for execu tion of the project and the rest of the 
amount was kept by the Trust with them. ITDC transf erred an amount of Rs. 55.00 lakhs to 
the AC Division and kept the remaining amount of Rs .4.81 crore for civil works. ITDC has so 
far submitted UCs for an amount of Rs. 3.93 crore t owards civil works which means that a 
sum of Rs.1.43 crore is still available with ITDC.  In addition, a sum of Rs.2.15 crore is 
available with Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial T rust (JBNMT) for which UCs has not 
been submitted. 
Further funds to Jallianwala Bagh National Memorial  Trust (JBNMT) can be 
released only after submission of the UCs for the e ntire amount which had been released to 
them earlier.  Since UCs for an amount of about Rs. 3.58 crore are still pending form JBNMT, 
no funds were released to them during 2014-15 out of Rs. 1.00 lakh under plan. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
154.  The Committee notes the reply. 
Vacancies in various Organizations under the Ministry  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
155. The Committee takes serious view of the large number of vacancies existing in ASI 
at all levels from a very long time. Although ASI h as taken steps to get its lapsed posts 
revived, the Committee strongly feels that ASI shou ld urgently step up its efforts to fill up the 
vacancies in a time bound manner.  The Ministry sho uld regularly monitor the progress made 
in this regard and furnish a detailed reply to the Committee.  
                                                                                                (Para No. 123 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
156. Regular action is being taken to fill the vaca ncies in different cadres of 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).  For this pur pose Staff Selection Commission (SSC) 
and Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) have bee n requested regularly.  Prompt action 
is also being taken to fill vacancies through promo tion.   Department Promotion Committee 
meeting is held regularly by ASI and UPSC for this purpose.   In the last one year 220 posts 
have been filled through direct recruitment/promotion.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
157.  The Committee notes the reply. The Committee would  like to know the status 
of the comprehensive cadre review undertaken in ASI. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
158. As regards non- availability of people of requ ired qualification particularly for 
technical posts, the Committee reiterates its earli er recommendation to consider running 
training institutions in required field, for encour aging people by offering lucrative career 
prospects and payments.  
    (Para No. 124 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
159. In order to equip the technical manpower with latest know-how, Archaeological 
Survey of India (ASI) has adopted the Human Resourc e Development (HRD) Policy which 
provides for collaboration with Universities, Techn ical Institutions, Organizations of Inter-
national repute for training course at all levels. The cultural exchange programme with various 

countries also provides for upgradation of the skil l of technical manpower.  HRD Policy 
(Institute of Archaeology) has been uploaded on the ASI website. 
   Recruitment Rules (RRs) for the post of Director , Centre for Cultural Resources 
and Training (CCRT) have been approved by the Ministry and will be notified shortly. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
160.  The Committee notes the reply. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
161. The Committee notes the unfilled vacancies exi sting in various Organisations.  The 
Committee is constrained to note that many of the v acancies which exist are at the level of 
Heads of the Organisations.  The Committee has seri ous concerns as this would adversely 
affect the functioning of these Organisations. The Committee recommends that the Ministry 
should take urgent steps to ensure that these vacancies are filled up without further delay.  The 
Committee impresses upon the Ministry that it shoul d co-ordinate with UPSC and other 
concerned authorities to ensure that the delays and  bottlenecks in this regard are cleared. The 
Committee also desires tha 
t the process of finalizing Recruitment Rules should be speeded up.                                                 
                         (Para No. 127 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
162. 
 Regular action is being taken to fill the vacancies  in different cadres of 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).  For this pur pose, Staff Selection Commission (SSC) 
and Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) have bee n requested regularly.    Prompt 
action is also being taken to fill vacancies throug h promotion.   In the last one year 220 posts 
have been filled through direct recruitment/promotion.   As a result of constant follow up with 
UPSC, recruitment rules in respect of Jt. Director Generals have been approved.  The post of 
Addl. Director General has already been advertised.  The Recruitment process is under way. 
Action is underway for filling up the vacant posts of Member Secretary, Indira 
Gandhi National Centre for Arts (IGNCA) and Directo r, Centre for Cultural Resources and 
Training (CCRT).  
  The post of Director General, National Archives of India was advertised on 
28.03.2015. With the approval of the Hon’ble Minist er of Culture, PMO has been requested 
for the nomination of three experts by the Hon’ble PM for the Search-cum-Selection 
committee headed by Cabinet Secretary.  
The post of director, Anthropological Survey of Ind ia was advertised on 6 th  
September, 2014. The Search-cum-Selection Committee  which met on 30 th  March, 2015 
under the chairmanship of Cabinet Secretary observe d that in regard to the Ph. D. Degrees 
held by some of the applicants, a clarification was  required to be sought from the Ministry of 
Human Resource Development as to whether the same c ould be accepted as equivalent to a 
Doctorate in Anthropology as specified in the notif ied Recruitment Rules of the aforesaid 
post. As per the observations of the Search-cum-Sel ection Committee, Ministry of Human 
Resource Development has been requested on 22 nd  April, 2015 to provide certain 
clarifications followed by D.O. letters, latest on 22.06.2015. 
Advertisement has been issued for filling up the po st of Director General, National 
Museum. Advertisements for filling up of the vacant posts of Additional Director General and 
Joint Director General in the National Museum will be issued shortly. Search-Cum-Selection-
Committee for filling up the post of Director Gener al, National Gallery of Modern Arts 

(NGMA) is being set up and its meeting is being fix ed shortly. Regarding filling up the post 
of Directors in NGMA, Bengaluru and Mumbai proposal  for filling up the posts on direct 
Recruitment basis has been submitted to UPSC and UP SC has informed that the post would 
be advertised in July, 2015.  Recruitment Rules of all the Gazetted posts in NGMA have been 
notified and in respect of other posts these are at  various stages of finalization. Advertisement 
for the post of Director, Salarjung Museum was issu ed and 16 applications were received by 
the due date (30.03.2015). One of the candidates ha s filed a writ Petition in CAT, Hyderabad. 
Therefore the matter is sub-judise.   
  Library Division is taking action on regular basi s to ensure time bound filling up of 
the vacant posts in the organizations under its adm inistrative control with greater emphasis on 
filling up the posts of Heads of Organizations. Als o, action is being taken for finalizing the 
Recruitment Rules, as applicable, on priority.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
163.  The Committee takes note of the reply furnished by  the Ministry. The 
Committee urges the Ministry that regular follow up  regarding filling up of vacancies 
should be done by the Ministry, with UPSC and SSC. The Ministry should ensure that 
anticipatory time bound action should be taken to e nsure that vacancies are filled up 
within a reasonable time span. The Ministry should also take necessary action to obviate 
delay in finalization of Recruitment Rules of the various posts. 
Zonal Cultural Centers 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
164. The Committee impresses upon the Ministry to e nsure that young talents in the 
cul 
tural field, especially from the rural areas, are identified and given necessary assistance.                                 
    (Para No. 129 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
165. All the Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) are impl ementing a scheme for Award to 
Young Talented Artistes under which ZCC identifies young promising talents in folk art and 
culture and  an amount of Rs. 10000/- and a certifi cate is given to them to enable them to 
realize their full potential. 
  Further, young talented artists participate in it s various programmes conducted 
through different schemes by ZCCs.   
Government of India, Ministry of Culture has recent ly enhanced the remuneration in respect 
of all folk artists as well as Gurus which include young artists also.   
 FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
166.  The Committee notes the reply. 
Buddhist Circuit 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
167. The Committee also finds a distinct lack of co -ordination among the concerned 
Union Ministries viz. , Culture, Tourism, Civil Aviation, Road Transport & Highways and that 
the Governments of Uttar Pradesh & Bihar.  As a res ult, we have not been able to have a 
concrete action plan for the development of these Buddhist Circuits by providing easy and fast 
connectivity - air and road, as also the required f acilities like affordable hotels, taxis, souvenir 
shops, restaurants, safety and security.            
    (Para No. 131 of ibid ) 

168. The Committee notes that many of the monuments /archaeological sites/places 
included in the Buddhist Circuits are protected by Archaeological Survey of India.  The 
Ministry of Culture has an added responsibility to ensure that Buddhist Circuits are developed 
in a better way to attract the tourists.  Therefore , the Committee recommends that an action 
plan in this regard should be chalked out without f urther delay. The Committee also urges the 
Ministry to have a formal mechanism to have an effe ctive co-ordination among the Ministry 
of Culture and Archaeological Survey of India, Mini stries of Tourism, Civil Aviation, Road 
Transport & Highways and the respective State Gover nments to ensure that all the Buddhist 
places are integrated seamlessly, well connected by  good roads, transportation, airports, 
safety, security etc. so that Buddhist tourists are  attracted to come in large numbers who are 
not coming now mainly because we do not have these facilities. It will earn enough respect as 
also revenue for us apart from commercial benefits to the stakeholders, big and small.              
    (Para No. 132 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
169. A comprehensive plan for Buddhist Circuits is being developed by Ministry of 
Tourism in consultation with various Stake holders including Archaeological Survey of India. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
170.  The Committee may be apprised of the updated statu s of the comprehensive 
plan for Buddhist Circuits and the timeframe within  which it would be finalized to take 
steps to implement the same, in the Action Taken Note. 
Other issues 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
171. The Committee strongly recommends that the Min istry may expedite the 
conservation activities undertaken at present in th e above cited places and also approach the 
concerned State Archaeology Departments for taking initiatives for their preservation, upkeep 
etc. to attract tourists as they have large potential in this regard.  
                                                                                      (Para No. 134 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
172. A new Conservation Policy of Archaeological Su rvey of India (ASI) has been 
adopted and all protected monuments are maintained as per its provision.   All SAs have been 
directed to ensure that all tourist amenities are u pgraded to the desired level expeditiously.  A 
few of the following sites / monuments, which are o f significance in the Buddhist circuits,

ii) Piprahwa and Ganwaria (Ancient Kapilvastu) 
iii) Vikramshila monaster, Antichak, Distt. Bhagalpur

v) Nalanda 
vi) Sarnath 
vii) Kushinagar

ix) Aurangabad Caves  

x) Ellora Caves, Aurangabad; and  
xi) Ruined Buddhist Stupa, Amarvati etc. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
173.  The Committee notes the reply. 
National Mission for Manuscripts  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
174. One of the Members of the Committee suggested that the ancient Sanskrit taxts and 
handwritten books in the Sadhu Ashram, Hoshiarpur a nd Bhrigu Samhita which is an

)

    (Para No. 136 of ibid )

 176. The National Mission on Manuscripts had opened  a Manuscript Resource Centre

REPORT  
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action T aken by the Ministry of Road Transport 
and Highways on the observations/recommendations as  contained in its Two Hundred and Twentieth 
Report on Demands for Grants 2015-16 of the Road Transport and Highways which was presented to both 
the Houses of Parliament on 28 th  April, 2015. 
2.  Action Taken Replies were received from the Min istry in respect of all the 
observations/recommendations contained in the Report have been categorized as follows:– 
(i) Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government: 
Paragraph Nos. 8,18,49,52,96,110,157        
(ii)  Recommendations/Observations which the Commit tee does not desire to pursue in view of the 
Government replies:– 
Paragraph Nos.19,31,43,47,48,50,53,54,55,56,61,65,7 0,79,84,89,107,116,121,133,136,139,141,142, 143, 
      
(iii) Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been accepted 
by the Committee: 
       
(iv) Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still awaited. 
      
3. The Committee desires that final replies in respect  of those recommendations/observations which 
have been categorized as interim replies by the Committee should be furnished at the earliest. 
4.     On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the  Committee has made Observations on each item of 
Action taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry. The recommendations of the Committee contained in 
the Two Hundred Twentieth Report, action taken ther eon by the Ministry and 
recommendations/Observations of the Committee on ea ch item of action taken has been given in the 
succeeding paragraphs: 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS   OF THE COMMITTEE 
5.     The Committee finds that the allocations for  the Ministry were reduced at RE stage for its 
programmes and projects as in the past. But while t he Ministry was able to spend 96.82% allocations 
during the year 2014-15, it could spend only 91.25%  during 2013-14. The Committee feels that the 
reduction of allocation of funds for this important  infrastructure sector at RE stage should be avoide d 
particularly when the expenditure percentage has be en very good. The Committee strongly recommends 
that the Ministry should take up this issue with the Ministry of Finance.                    
      (Recommendation at Para 5  of the 220 th  Report) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
6.     Noted for compliance.  The issue will be tak en up with Ministry of Finance at appropriate time.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
7.     The Committee notes the reply of the Ministr y and further requests them to apprise the 
response to be received from the Ministry of Finance on this issue to the Committee. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS   OF THE COMMITTEE 
8.     The reasons submitted by the Ministry for un der-utilization of funds under some 
schemes/programmes are of routine nature. The Commi ttee feels that proper planning, timely monitoring 
and taking preventing steps anticipating the routin e bottlenecks would ensure timely completion of 
schemes/projects and programmes. The Committee desi res that shortcomings with regard to 
implementation of projects may be identified in con sultation with the stakeholders involved in road 
Paragraph Nos. : 51
144,145, 146,147,148,149,150,151,152,153,154,155,156
Paragraph Nos: 5,9,11,20,71,86,90,95,97,103,112,128

projects so that such things are not repeated in fu ture. The Committee hopes that the spending pattern  of 
the Ministry will see an improvement in the coming years. 
 (Para 8  of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
9.     The Observations of the Committee noted for compliance.  However, due emphasis is being given i n 
the quality of project preparation ensuring that th ey reflect ground realities and considering previou s 
experiences.  Further, periodic review meetings are  held at various levels to monitor the progress of 
project, identify bottlenecks and take up necessary  corrective action for expediting progress of proje cts.   
In this regard, consultations are also held with va rious stakeholders during project preparation, 
implementation, and for identification of major bottlenecks resolving them, etc.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
10.    The Committee notes the reply and hopes that  with the existing co-ordination mechanism and 
consultations with the stakeholders, the Ministry will be able to improve its spending pattern during 
the current fiscal.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS   OF THE COMMITTEE 
11.    The Committee finds that the Ministry was no t able to utilize Rs.22.20 crore provided from the 
Central Road Fund for State roads in Delhi for the year 2014-15. Though this fund is non-lapsable, the  
reasons submitted by the Ministry for non-utilizati on due to less number of proposals received from th e 
Delhi Government are not impressive. The Committee hopes that the Ministry should impress upon the 
State Governments in such cases to send their propo sals in time so that the allocated funds could be s pent 
fully. 
 (Para 9 
 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
12.        All the State Governments have been advi sed to submit their proposal for development of Sta te 
roads under Central Road Fund timely.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
13.      The Committee notes the reply of the Minis try; but the Committee wants to know further as 
to the reasons why the State Governments fail to send their proposals in time. 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS   OF THE COMMITTEE 
14.      The Committee appreciates the Ministry’s c oncern in this regard. However, the Committee notes  
that the Ministry did not actively pursue the matte r with the Ministry of Finance as could be understo od 
from the reply furnished by the Ministry to the rec ommendations made by the Committee in its 193rd 
Report in this regard. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should pursue the issue of removal of 
ceiling of expenditure for the last quarter with th e Ministry of Finance vigorously. The Committee urg es 
upon the Ministry of Finance to consider the remova l on ceiling of expenditure for road projects durin g 
the last quarter. It will help the Ministry of Road  Transport and Highways to spend the allocation ful ly 
and also to complete the projects in time without cost overrun. 
 (Para 11 
 of ibid ) 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
15.     This Ministry has been consistently taking up the need for relaxation of Scheme-wise restricti on of 
33% of total expenditure for the last quarter and 1 5% in the last month considering the less working 
season for road works in the country due to long du ration of monsoon and snow fall in hilly areas.   

However, matter will be taken up with Ministry of F inance during the last quarter of the financial yea r 
after reviewing the expenditure.  
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE 
16. The Committee feels that unless the ceiling on spending of funds during the last quarter is 
not removed, the Ministry will not be able to spend  much of the allocated funds.  The Committee, 
therefore, reiterates its recommendation that the M inistry should pursue this issue with the 
Ministry of Finance vigorously.  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS   OF THE COMMITTEE 
17. The Committee is pleasantly surprised to find t hat the Ministry was able to get Rs. 82,697.15 
crore (including IEBR) as against its projected dem and of Rs. 54,692.49 crore (including IEBR) for the  
year 2015-16. The Committee also finds that the GBS  component for the Ministry has seen an increase 
from Rs. 26,288.00 crore in 2014-15 (BE) to Rs. 40, 655.65 crore (BE) in 2015-16 which is a good

36. During the last 3 years, the highways sector is  going through a difficult phase. Public Private 
Partnership (PPP) projects through Build Operate Tr ansfer (BOT) (Toll) mode are not able to attract bi ds. 
Major highway developers in the country which are l imited in number have capacity constraints includin g 
over-leveraged financials due to excessive exposure  to infrastructure projects including highways. 
Another inherent issue for the sector is lack of av ailability of debt products aligned with revenue st ream 
profile of highway projects resulting in financial stress in projects during the initial construction years. In 
addition, there have been issues like some banks re aching the ceiling as per sectoral exposure norms. 
Quite a few projects have got stalled in the construction stage due to these reasons. These are discouraging 
prospective bidders to participate in new project bids.  
37. In order to revive the Highways Sector and to e xpedite the implementation of road projects, this 
Ministry has taken following steps: 
(a) With the constant interaction with Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change, a number o f 
specific bottlenecks for speedy execution of National Highways Projects have been resolved.  
(b) Three meetings of the Group of Infrastructure h eaded by Hon’ble Minister (RT&H,S) have 
been held and a number of inter-Ministerial issues have been resolved. 
(c)  Government on 13.05.2015 has approved the poli cy which permits 100 % equity divestment 
after two years of construction completion for all BOT projects irrespective of year of award. This wo uld 
facilitate infusion of liquidity in the sector by e nabling existing developers to release their locked -in 
equity in completed projects. Out of the 115 Conces sion Agreements signed up to 30 
th  September, 2009 
on BOT (Toll) and BOT (Annuity), 80 such projects h ave been completed, and the locked in equity of 
such completed projects works out to approximately Rs.4500 crores. This amount of equity by itself 
would be able to support construction of an estimat ed length of around 1500 kms of projects on PPP 
mode. 

(d) Government on 13.05.2015 has also approved the policy for one time fund infusion to revive 
and physically complete languishing BOT projects. F or any languishing highway project in BOT (Toll) 
mode that has achieved at least 50% physical comple tion and it is also established that infusion of 
moderate funding can quickly bring this project to completion, NHAI will provide financial assistance to 
such a project from the overall budget corpus of NH AI on loan basis for a short tenure and with a pre-
determined return.  This assistance (say bridge fun d) will be provided on a loan basis at Bank Rate +2 % 
drawing a parallel with the provisions of the Model  Concession Agreement. This proposal would help 
physical completion of languishing projects bringin g relief thereby, to the citizens /highway users in  the 
area. 
(e)  This Ministry has also adopted a new Hybrid An nuity model for implementation of highway 
projects in order to encourage private sector parti cipation through adequate incentives. The objective  is to 
maximize the quantum of implemented highway project s within available financial resources of the 
Government. As per this model, 40% the Project Cost  is to be provided by the Government as 
‘Construction Support’ to the private developer dur ing the construction period and the balance 60% as 
annuity payments over  the concession period along with interest on outstanding amount to the 
concessionaire. There is separate provision for O&M  payments by the Government to the concessionaire. 
The private party does not have to bear the traffic  risk. All the payments have been inflation indexed  by a 
Price Multiple Index which is a weighted average of WPI and CPI (IW) on 70:30 bases. This mitigates the 
inflation risk for the developer.

Transport & Highways for several years has observed  that while Highway construction has become its 
main thrust area, its attention to Road Transport a nd Safety remains woefully inadequate. The Committe e 
understands the practical constraints in this regar d and emphasizes the need for keeping all kinds of 
extraneous forces/lobbies at bay in implementing an d enforcing transport and road safety laws in the 
Country.

196. Recommendation of the Committee has been noted  for consideration.
